dimensions.summary: The logged-in product is structurally sound (URL-per-screen with working browser back, focus-trapped modals, undo on task/archive actions, good offline and failed-save handling, working CSV/ICS/packet exports, a complete submit → accept → next-cycle lifecycle) but it is not launchable as-is: any second keystroke in the log-activity sheet unmounts the whole app (all five controlled fields read event.currentTarget inside a state updater), Sign out for real accounts points at a dead /signout-with-chatgpt URL, credentials can never be edited or deleted, and after a renewal is accepted Home's hero shows the closed cycle with a live countdown. Beyond those P1s, the experience reads as an iPhone app: one-credential hero with no multi-credential overview, 19–25-control "Quick add" sheet whose Save button sits below the fold on a 900px desktop, jargon-heavy regulatory copy (20-word check-in titles, "classification gaps", "countable units"), seven different labels for the same log action, stale "Today" tab references, and gamification (Levels/XP/weekly quests) occupying prime dashboard space for a compliance audience. First-credential setup is the biggest conversion wall: a 170-option native select, empty dates with server-only rules ("expiration must be March 31"), and a jargon attestation checkbox with no inline validation feedback. All exploration was done against the local dev app; the demo user's data is unchanged (one checklist toggle was undone), while a throwaway identity app-ux-new@example.test now holds four test credentials that cannot be removed from the UI (see app-ux-03). Screenshots and scripts are under the scratchpad app-ux/ and pw/ directories.

The public funnel is fast and self-contained (7.7 KB landing, zero external requests, 138 ms TTFB, prod byte-identical to the repo files) and the auth backend is soundly engineered (scrypt, hashed single-use tokens, HMAC-signed HttpOnly/Secure/Lax cookie, Origin-based CSRF check, per-IP rate limits). But in production the funnel is non-functional end to end: verification email is unconfigured, the only contact address (support@itrackceu.com) has no MX and bounces, the "contact us" dead-end has no link, unverified accounts are purged after 7 days, and the web app's only Sign out control points at a 404 route from the old hosting platform. The iOS-shell compromises now actively damage the web product: the Safari/Firefox UA gate and the 401 Basic challenge deny the landing page to Google's inspection/verification tools, every social/link-preview bot, AI crawlers, SEO tools and uptime monitors, and hand browser fetches a native Basic-auth popup; robots.txt, sitemap, favicon, OG image and manifest all 303 to /login. Landing copy still sells beta, ads and a $9.99 Pro tier, says nothing about who the product is for (53 professions, 170 source-linked templates, 98 issuing bodies), offers no trust signals, privacy policy or terms, and every CTA fails WCAG AA contrast. Gateway-level fixes (drop UA/Basic gating, public static allowlist, real logout, email + DNS, privacy/terms pages) must ship regardless of and before the redesign; the visual, copy and a11y items are the redesign's acceptance criteria.

The logged-in app is in unusually good accessibility shape for an 11k-line single-file client: axe (wcag2a/aa, 2.1, 2.2, best-practice) reports 0 violations across all 32 app runs (Home, Credentials, Credential detail, History, Profile, plus the Log activity sheet, the Set up a credential sheet and the Due-date check-ins sheet, at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark); the shared Modal has a real focus trap with inert siblings, Escape and focus restore; every pointer target is ≥44px except native checkboxes/radios that sit inside ≥44px labels; reduced-motion collapses every transition/animation to 0.01ms; text-spacing and 200%-zoom (720px) reflow are clean; and my own rendered-background contrast sampling of the 248 nodes axe left "incomplete" (gradient hero, translucent pills, dark scheme) found every one passing except text on the dimmed under-screen. The real defects are concentrated in shell logic rather than styling: the pushed credential-detail screen leaves the list screen underneath focusable and readable (three hidden tab stops and a second H1 before the back button), the Modal drops focus to body on close for every sheet that contains a React autoFocus field (18/18 cases: Set up a credential, Add task, Log submission), and the SPA never changes document.title or announces route changes. The public pages are the launch risk: every primary CTA and text link on landing/login/signup/reset/verify fails AA contrast (white on #007aff 4.02:1, #007aff on the grey page 3.60:1 — the app already fixed this with --accent-control, the pages did not), inputs have a 1.28:1 boundary, and the landing has no main landmark, a heading jump and colour-only links; prod serves byte-identical files so these apply to itrackceu.com today. Cross-cutting items to carry into the redesign: a ≥3:1 input boundary and a real 3px focus ring on fields, a consistent inline error pattern (today validation is native bubbles only), rem-based type, and urgency expressed in words rather than dot colour. Side effect: my toast probe snoozed one demo reminder (no UI or API exists to un-snooze); I deleted only that row (id e6c1557a…) from the Miniflare D1 SQLite state and verified the inbox is back to 2 check-ins; two other reminder_states rows written at 13:23 UTC predate any mutating step of mine and were left untouched.

Load performance of the production build is good and the bottleneck is bytes on slow networks, not CPU: the shell is 13.4 KB HTML (2.8 KB gz) + 97 KB CSS (19 KB gz) + 496 KB JS in 5 chunks (142 KB gz), 9 requests / 224 KB wire on a cold load; on an unthrottled desktop the trace shows FCP 46 ms, hydrated 47 ms, workspace data painted 65 ms, LCP 97 ms with zero long tasks, and on a 4x-throttled CPU + Fast-3G profile FCP 780 ms (skeleton), hydrated 1,291 ms, data painted 1,512 ms, LCP 1,565 ms, main thread busy only ~600 ms. Assets are immutable+gzip+ETag (verified on the identical build under workerd, and gzip pass-through verified on prod via /api/widget-summary), tesseract.js is lazy (7 KB gz chunk; 4.45 MB of core+language only on first scan, then SW-cached), no webfonts load, and the Railway proxy adds negligible overhead (healthz TTFB 175-257 ms ≈ landing TTFB 157-255 ms from NYC; per-request session SQLite cost measured 0.02 ms). The dist/ I inspected is from Aug 12 08:22:24 2026, i.e. HEAD 3f477e6 (app source last changed 2026-08-11), so it is current. The material problems are elsewhere: typing normally into the Log-activity title field crashes the whole app to a blank page on the production build (a functional setState updater reads event.currentTarget after dispatch), the PWA offline fallback is broken (precached /offline.html is a 307 redirect so offline navigation ends in net::ERR_FAILED), a 57 KB PNG favicon plus ~397 KB of SW precache compete with the critical JS on mobile, the template catalog is 702 KB decoded (95 KB gz) for a chooser that needs ~48 KB, and ~181 KB of dead Manrope/Newsreader woff2 ship in the build. Ranked by user-visible gain per effort: (1) fix the updater crash, (2) fix the offline precache path, (3) tiny favicon + optimized icons + long cache headers + trim precache, (4) slim catalog endpoint, (5) per-screen code splitting and critical CSS during the redesign (~0.5 s on Fast 3G), (6) server-fetch or preload the workspace JSON to remove the post-hydration waterfall (~0.2 s), (7) OCR prefetch/size disclosure, (8) font budget/strategy for the new display face, (9) gateway/landing hygiene. I could not find the referenced "SSR/first-paint waterfall (architectural)" deferred note in docs/ or git history (the only explicit deferral is the Stripe/ads Phase 2), but the waterfall itself is real and measured.

The core authorization model is solid: the Railway gateway strips client-supplied oai-*/identity headers and injects a trusted identity, every workspace and evidence query in route.ts/db/runtime.ts is parameterized and scoped to user_id = identity.userId (the handful of ${} SQL interpolations are compile-time constants or ?-placeholder builders), client-supplied userId is rejected, sessions rotate on login and are killed on password reset, passwords use scrypt+salt with a dummy-hash existence-oracle guard, and the internal cron route is double-gated. Evidence upload validation (magic bytes, size, filename sanitization, key built from validated ids) and the CSRF posture on the JSON command endpoint are genuinely good. The most serious issue is the widget feed: it bypasses gateway auth, is gated only by one shared static token that shipped in the (now-retired) iOS binaries, always serves the OLDEST account's credential names/deadlines/progress regardless of who calls, and I confirmed the token is configured in production (401, not 503) — a live cross-tenant PII exposure. Secondary issues are the total absence of security headers in prod (no HSTS/CSP/X-Frame-Options/Referrer-Policy/Permissions-Policy), a verify-by-GET flow that both burns the single-use token and mints a session (mail-scanner hostile), account enumeration on signup/login, a 5-minute Basic-auth cache that honors old credentials after a reset, and a rate-limiter whose correctness rests on an unverified assumption about Railway's x-forwarded-for ordering. Retiring the iOS shell cleanly removes the two biggest attack-surface items (the widget bearer exemption and Basic auth entirely).

The client is one 10,953-line file whose shell component `ITrackApp()` (lines 1656–6511, 4,856 lines) holds 43 useState / 10 useRef / 19 useEffect / 10 useMemo / 11 useCallback plus 45 inner functions, and renders 9 modals inline that close over 4–38 shell identifiers each; the five screens and the allocators are already prop-driven leaf components (TodayView 1,017 lines/23 props, CredentialDetailScreen 428/13, RecordsView 347/11, AccountView 458/15), so they can move verbatim, but the modals, the single global `error` string (54 setError sites), the shared FORM pending key and the hidden `selectedCredentialId` subject have to be redesigned into explicit props/hooks. The code itself is healthy — tsc and eslint are clean, contrast-audit passes 98 claims, there are no TODOs, and the event.currentTarget-after-await bug count is zero (all 8 async handlers capture synchronously) — but it is coupled to the retired platforms: a broken `/signout-with-chatgpt` sign-out link (404), Capacitor haptics, 3,747 lines of APNs/widget code, a gateway User-Agent gate that exists only for the WKWebView, and a literal "L" (License Lantern) glyph on every empty state. `globals.css` (6,618 lines, 145 tokens, 653+180 rule blocks) is not dead-heavy (0 unused class selectors, 2 unused tokens) but is cross-cut: every screen's responsive rules live in four trailing media blocks and 44 selectors are declared twice, and `tools/contrast-audit.mjs` assumes a single file. The biggest brake on decomposition is the test suite: 165 of the 2,189 assertions in `tests/rendered-html.test.mjs` are regexes over the *source text* of ITrackApp.tsx (125) and globals.css (40) across 16 subtests, plus a build-chunk lookup by the `ITrackApp-` filename prefix, so any file move fails `npm test` until those pins are re-pointed or replaced. The full inventory, shared-state model, 10-step extraction order, per-section CSS map and pin-by-subtest table are in ARCHITECTURE-INVENTORY.md; the 12,504-line `app/api/workspace/route.ts` (134 functions, 23-action switch) is the server-side twin of this problem and is why the client hand-mirrors 13 API types.

The iOS shell touches this repo in four layers. (1) The Railway gateway's Basic-auth path, the "Safari/|Firefox/" UA gate and the widget-feed bypass are the only layer that actively hurts the public web product today: on itrackceu.com they 401 iOS in-app browsers (Gmail/LinkedIn/Facebook/Instagram), social link previewers, AI crawlers and every PWA asset including /manifest.webmanifest (which Chrome fetches without cookies, so prod is not installable), and they answer expired-session API calls with a raw browser Basic prompt. (2) A fully wired, live APNs channel (five APNS_* vars plus ITRACK_WIDGET_TOKEN set on Railway, ~3.8k lines, 43 tests, two D1 tables, a cron fan-out every 15 minutes) that does nothing for web users. (3) Client-side native-feel code, of which only the window.Capacitor haptics lookup and the JS edge-swipe are shell-only; the history-backed nav stack, route pages, manifest/service worker/offline page, web push (VAPID), the iOS-Safari install helpers and safe-area/zoom rules are genuine web needs that must survive the sweep, while the tab bar, sheets, push header and press states are redesign inputs. (4) Rationale baked into comments, README, Dockerfile, DESIGN-SYSTEM.md (the "no webfont because Capacitor" rule) and TC-002. All six protected identifiers are commented as load-bearing but nothing tests them. Safe order is code-before-env: create Chris's same-email web account (blocked today because RESEND_API_KEY/AUTH_EMAIL_FROM are unset), ship the gateway PR, then delete ITRACK_USERS/ITRACK_WIDGET_TOKEN, then the worker/db PR, then APNS_* and the Apple key, then client/doc cleanup; itrack-shell:// handling and Capacitor imports do not exist in this repo.

The edge is in decent shape: itrackceu.com resolves (A 69.46.46.121, Railway "Hikari" edge, custom domain verified via _railway-verify TXT), TLS is a Let's Encrypt ECDSA cert (valid to 2026-11-10, auto-renewed, TLS 1.2/1.3 only, chain OK), HTTP→HTTPS 301 preserves path+query, workerd gzips app responses, and sessions/cookie secret live on the volume so users stay logged in across deploys. Everything around it that a public launch depends on is unfinished: no Resend DNS records or keys (sign-up cannot be completed, reset mail cannot be sent), no MX for support@, www is NXDOMAIN, the apex is a hand-coded A record to one of several interchangeable edge IPs, no CAA/DNSSEC, no HSTS or any security header, and the gateway's User-Agent gate (kept only for the retiring iOS shell) answers 401 Basic to link-preview bots, AI crawlers, uptime monitors, HEAD requests and every iOS in-app browser, while robots/sitemap/favicon/og.png redirect to /login. Operationally the entire dataset (miniflare D1 SQLite, R2 blobs, auth.db, cookie secret) sits on a single Railway volume with no evidence of any backup, no health check or uptime monitoring, no CI (no .github at all, main auto-deploys), an abrupt SIGTERM exit, and a 15-minute in-process cron capped at 8 pushes/64 subscriptions per run that stops entirely if Serverless is ever enabled. Security hygiene needs attention: a 20-char Basic-auth password for the chris account is committed in the PUBLIC cskerritt/iTrack repo, ITRACK_OPEN_IDENTITY can disable auth with one variable, and raw verify/reset links are logged whenever mail fails (which is always, today). Retiring iOS lets APNS_* (5 vars), ITRACK_WIDGET_TOKEN, ITRACK_USERS/VIGILO_USERS/LANTERN_USERS, ITRACK_OPEN_IDENTITY, Basic auth, the widget exemption, the APNs stack and the UA gate all be deleted; the true launch blockers are email (infra-01), backups (infra-04) and the leaked credential (infra-03).

findings.title: Log-activity sheet crashes the whole app on the second keystroke in any text field (known Credits-earned bug confirmed, and wider)
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:4523 (title), :4551 (completionDate), :4593 (totalUnits / Credits earned), :4632 (allocatedUnits), :4751 (provider) — event.currentTarget.value read inside setActivityDraft(updater)
findings.evidence: Playwright, desktop 1440x900, light: open Log activity, click Credits earned, type "12.5" → console TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value') at ITrackApp.tsx (compiled 3149:52) → basicStateReducer; React 19 unmounts the root and the body is left with only the RSC bootstrap script (blank page; Vite overlay in dev, screenshot 04-bug-b-type-credits-fresh.png). 7/7 typing paths crashed (type, pressSequentially, backspace-edit, credits→allocated). Matrix: one keystroke in any field survives (React eager-state path), the second change in the sheet crashes — including a paste-style fill of a second field 2.5 s later. Title, provider and completion-date fields crash the same way; the uncontrolled Edit-record modal (FormData) does not. HEAD 3f477e6 equals origin/main and prod auto-deploys from main, and the pattern predates the 2026-07-27 rename, so production has it.
findings.impact: Every real user who types a course title longer than one character loses the app to a blank page mid-entry; the browser draft is restored on reload but the product looks broken at the single most important moment.
findings.recommendation: In all five handlers read the value synchronously before the updater (const value = event.currentTarget.value; setActivityDraft(current => ({...current, title: value}))). Add a top-level React error boundary with a "reload" recovery so a render error can never blank the page. Add a Playwright test that types two characters into each sheet field.
findings.verifier_note: Reproduced 3/3 ways in Chrome 1440x900 (pw/v-appux-01-crash.mjs): typing '12.5' in Credits earned, 'Et' in Title, and fill(title) then fill(provider) 2.5 s later each throw TypeError 'Cannot read properties of null (reading value)' at basicStateReducer and unmount <main> (body left with ~1084 chars of bootstrap text). A single keystroke survives (React eager-state path). Source confirmed: all five onChange handlers read event.currentTarget.value inside setActivityDraft updaters (ITrackApp.tsx:4523, 4551, 4593, 4632, 4751). No error boundary exists anywhere under app/ (no error.tsx, no componentDidCatch). One correction: the draft is not auto-restored on reload — the sheet stays closed; the typed title comes back only when the user reopens Log activity (with the 'Saved in this browser' note). Screens: app-ux-verify/01-crash-A-credits.png, 01-crash-B-title.png, 01-crash-E-after-reload.png.

findings.title: Sign out for real accounts points at a dead /signout-with-chatgpt URL
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:9255-9263 (Sign out); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:190-240 (only POST /auth/logout exists); deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:130-260 (no signout handling)
findings.evidence: Non-demo user (throwaway identity app-ux-new@example.test) sees a Sign out button on Profile whose href is /signout-with-chatgpt (screenshot 11-new-profile-desktop.png). Local GET of that path → 404 from the worker. On prod, unauthenticated browser GET https://itrackceu.com/signout-with-chatgpt → 303 /login (gateway has no such route; a signed-in request would be proxied to the worker's 404), and GET /auth/logout → 404 (POST only). The demo user never sees the button, so local testing hides it.
findings.impact: Signed-in users cannot sign out at all; on a shared or clinic computer the session cookie stays live, and the 404 page reads as a broken product.
findings.recommendation: Replace the anchor with a same-origin POST form to /auth/logout (button styled as today), or add a GET /auth/logout handler in the gateway that clears the cookie and 303s to /. Also add display-name/email/password change and account deletion to Profile — none exist today for a self-serve account.
findings.verifier_note: ITrackApp.tsx:9257-9263 renders <a href='/signout-with-chatgpt?return_to=%2F'> for every non-demo user (seen live as app-ux-new@example.test; it is a plain anchor, not a form). gateway.mjs has no such route and auth-routes.mjs:190-192 404s anything that is not a POST to /auth/{signup,login,logout,request-reset,reset,resend}. Local GET of the href with identity headers → 404 from the worker; prod GET with a Safari UA (unauthenticated) /signout-with-chatgpt → 303 /login and /auth/logout → 404. Sessions are SQLite-backed with SESSION_TTL_MS = 30 days (auth.mjs:14), so a shared-computer session stays live for a month with no way to end it.

findings.title: A credential can never be edited or deleted — a wrong template or date is permanent
findings.location: app/api/workspace/route.ts action switch (~12380; actions: createCredential, addActivity, … — no updateCredential/deleteCredential/archiveCredential); app/ITrackApp.tsx:7938-8367 CredentialDetailScreen has no edit/remove control
findings.evidence: Full workspace action list (createCredential, addActivity, addActivityAllocation, archiveActivity, archivePersonalTask, claimWeeklyQuest, createPersonalTask, markRenewalAccepted, markSubmitted, restoreActivity, restorePersonalTask, saveDentalCheckpoint, setReminderState, toggleTask, updateActivity, updateActivityAllocationRequirements, updatePersonalTask, updateReminderPreferences, updateRequirementApplicability, updateWeeklyGoal) contains nothing that mutates or removes a credential. The detail screen's controls are: Prepare packet, Configure check-ins, Add date to calendar, Open official guidance, Log submission. The throwaway user's test credentials ("app-ux test", "app-ux test 2") cannot be removed; templates enforce exact dates at creation (NREMT: "expiration must be March 31", route.ts:1346; CRC: "exact five-year certification period", route.ts:1485), so a typo is unrecoverable except by creating a duplicate that also lives on Home forever.
findings.impact: Dead end for self-serve strangers (wrong state/template on first try is common with 170 templates), blocks data-deletion requests, and pollutes Home/Credentials with mistakes.
findings.recommendation: Add Edit (name, jurisdiction, issuer, cycle dates, unit label) and Archive/Delete (with confirmation and undo where possible) on the credential detail screen, backed by updateCredential/archiveCredential actions; keep renewed cycles intact under history.
findings.verifier_note: Action switch at route.ts:12377-12459 contains createCredential plus activity/task/reminder/push actions only; grep for updateCredential|deleteCredential|archiveCredential|removeCredential|renameCredential across route.ts and ITrackApp.tsx returns nothing. Live control dump of the pushed detail screen (demo LCSW on desktop, throwaway NREMT at 390px): Credentials, Prepare credential packet, Configure renewal check-ins, Add renewal date to calendar, Open official guidance, Log submission — no edit/delete/remove/archive/rename control or wording anywhere. Date rules are server-side 409s at route.ts:1343-1349 (NREMT 'expiration must be March 31' / EMR Sept 30) and :1482-1488 (CRC exact five-year window). Keeping P1: for a self-serve stranger the first mistake is permanent and there is no data-deletion path at all.

findings.title: After a renewal is accepted, Home's hero shows the closed cycle with a live countdown
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:1949-1959 (default selection = soonest deadline across ALL credentials, including status "renewed"); :2390-2400 selectedCredential fallback
findings.evidence: Throwable user: recorded submission and acceptance on "app-ux test 2" (toast "Renewal accepted. Your next cycle is ready.", successor due Aug 16, 2028). A fresh session's Home then shows hero "RENEWED · app-ux test 2 · 7 DAYS TO RENEWAL · Due Sep 16, 2026 · 0 of 4 hours counted · 5% READY" and Best next action "Review the preserved record for this completed cycle" while four active credentials exist (screenshot 21-home-after-accept-fresh-desktop.png). Once Sep 16 passes the same card will read "N days overdue".
findings.impact: The first screen answers "what do I owe, by when" with a deadline that no longer applies (and soon a false overdue alarm) for every user immediately after their first renewal — the moment the product is supposed to feel resolved.
findings.recommendation: Default selection should exclude status "renewed" (prefer active with soonest deadline, then submitted); after markRenewalAccepted, point selection at result.id everywhere (it already does on the detail screen); never render a countdown for a renewed cycle — show "Renewed on <date>" instead.
findings.verifier_note: Fresh context as app-ux-new@example.test (pw/v-appux-02-newuser.mjs): /api/workspace returns four active credentials (deadlines 2027-03-31 … 2028-08-16) plus one status 'renewed' with deadline 2026-09-16; Home hero reads 'RENEWED · app-ux test 2 · 7 DAYS TO RENEWAL · Due Sep 16, 2026 · 0 of 4 hours counted · 5% READY' and Best next action 'Review the preserved record for this completed cycle' (app-ux-verify/04-home-newuser-fresh.png). Mechanism confirmed: ITrackApp.tsx:1949-1959 sorts ALL credentials by deadline with no status filter, and the selection is never persisted (no localStorage key), so although handleAcceptance sets selection to result.id in-session (:3597-3606) every reload regresses to the closed cycle. The countdown label at :7089-7093 has no renewed guard (nor does :8174 on the detail screen, which also shows 'RENEW BY Sep 16, 2026 · TIME LEFT 7 days' for the renewed cycle), so after Sep 16 it will read 'days overdue'.

findings.title: Home is a single-credential dashboard; other credentials are invisible except through check-ins
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:7029-7370 TodayView (renewal-hero + credit progress + checklist all bound to one `credential`); :7849-7938 CredentialsView
findings.evidence: Throwaway user with NREMT (due Mar 31 2027), app-ux test (due Sep 10 2027), CRC (due Sep 30 2027): Home showed only NREMT's hero, progress, checklist and quests; a text search of <main> for the other two names returned null (screenshot 13-new-home-3-desktop.png). The Credentials list row shows name, jurisdiction, status and a bare "13%" — no due date, no days left, no next step (01-credentials-desktop-light.png).
findings.impact: A professional with two or three licenses (the paying-attention persona) cannot see what is owed across all of them; the app silently picks one and hides the rest.
findings.recommendation: Make the Home spine a multi-credential board: one row per active credential with due date, days left, credits progress and the single next action; the detail screen carries the deep content. The Credentials list should show the same due-date/next-step columns.
findings.verifier_note: Throwaway Home with five credentials: a leaf-node text search finds NREMT only inside a check-in reminder row (urgency class 'soon', 'due Dec 1, 2026' — a check-in date, not its Mar 31 2027 deadline); 'Certified Rehabilitation Counselor' and the 30%-complete 'app-ux test' appear nowhere in <main>. Section dump: renewal-hero, reminder-inbox, next-action-card, progress-card, progression-card, checklist-card, recent-card — every one bound to the single selected credential. Credentials rows show only name · jurisdiction · status and a bare percentage.

findings.title: "Quick add" sheet is a 19-control form (25+ for NREMT/CRC) with Save below the fold on desktop
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:4340-4905 activity sheet (photo capture block, title, date, Credits earned, Credits to apply, credential select, RequirementPicker/NremtRequirementAllocator/CrcRequirementAllocator, provider, proof radios); app/globals.css:3920-3929 (.modal-card max-height 852px at 900px viewport)
findings.evidence: Dialog control dump for the LCSW credential: 19 labelled controls; NREMT: 20 inputs incl. 10 numeric requirement fields and a pediatric-overlap field; CRC: 16 incl. approval pathway select, program reference and a 50-word attestation checkbox. At 1440x900 the card is 852px tall and the Save button sits at y≈1228 (~400px of internal scrolling); on 390x844 the NREMT sheet scrolls 2775px. "Credits to apply to this credential" duplicates "Credits earned" for the common case, and the five requirement tiles each repeat "Choose only one activity type from this group" (05-log-activity-full-desktop-tall.png, 14-sheet-nremt-mid-desktop.png, 14-sheet-crc-mid-desktop.png, 19-m-sheet-nremt-mid.png).
findings.impact: Logging one course — the daily action — costs a scroll-and-hunt on desktop and three screens on mobile; the length also makes the second-keystroke crash (app-ux-01) more likely to hit after real effort.
findings.recommendation: Split into essentials (title, date, credits, credential) then categorise (requirements/allocators) as a second step or progressive disclosure; hide "credits to apply" behind "Counts less than the certificate?"; make the action row sticky at the bottom of the card; demote the scan block to a compact "Scan certificate" button once fields are shown.
findings.verifier_note: 1440x900, demo LCSW: .modal-card is 852px tall (y 24→876) and Save activity sits at y≈1427, well below the 900px fold (finder measured 1228 in a different state; conclusion unchanged); 15 form fields (2 file, title, completionDate, totalUnits, allocatedUnits, credentialId, 5 requirementIds, provider, 2 evidenceStatus) plus 3 buttons, action row position static (not sticky). 390x844 with NREMT selected: .modal-card scrollHeight 2777 vs clientHeight 791, 20 fields of which 11 numeric, Save at y=2759. Screens: app-ux-verify/06-sheet-1440x900.png, 06-m-nremt-sheet.png.

findings.title: First-credential setup is a wall: 170-option native select, empty dates, server-only rules, jargon attestation, no inline validation feedback
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:4960-5130 (Set up a credential modal: search + <select> of 170 templates, cycleStart/deadline date inputs, required officialDatesAttested checkbox); app/api/workspace/route.ts:1346 and :1485 (date rules enforced only at submit)
findings.evidence: Throwaway first run: picking the NREMT template shows a ~180-word regulatory paragraph, leaves both date fields empty, and requires ticking "I checked my National Registry dashboard — It assigns this 2025 NCCP level template, and the cycle start and fixed expiration entered above match the dashboard exactly." First submit with dates filled but box unticked did nothing visible in the DOM (native validation only; dialog stays open, no toast). With the box ticked, submit fails after the round trip with "National Registry EMT, AEMT, and Paramedic expiration must be March 31."; CRC fails with "requires the exact five-year certification period shown in CRCCCONNECT". Only the custom path succeeded first time (12-add-nremt-picked.png, 12c-add-nremt-bottom.png, 05-add-credential-template-desktop-tall.png).

findings.recommendation: Derive or constrain dates from the template (e.g. NREMT: pick expiration year → March 31 auto-filled; CRC: start date → valid-through auto-computed); validate inline before submit; replace the native select with a searchable list showing profession/state chips; collapse the rule text behind "Read the rule"; reword attestations in plain language ("These dates match my NREMT dashboard").

findings.title: Clicking the backdrop does not close sheets; Escape closes every open modal at once through a global handler

findings.title: Failed saves show two alerts at once and pass raw server strings through

findings.title: Save actions render non-JSON error responses (expired-session 401, proxy 502) as 'Unexpected token … is not valid JSON'
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:2614-2625 (runAction: await response.json() runs before the response.ok / content-type check); deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:211-215 (401 text/plain 'Authentication required' for requests without a browser text/html Accept)
findings.evidence: Intercepted POST /api/workspace with a 401 text/plain 'Authentication required' body — what the gateway returns to a fetch (Accept */*) once the 30-day session cookie has expired or been cleared — and submitted Add task: both the page banner and the modal read "Unexpected token 'A', \"Authentica\"... is not valid JSON" (pw/v-appux-05-misc.mjs). The GET path is handled well by contrast: a 401 on load shows 'Your sign-in needs to be refreshed.' with a 'Reload and sign in' button (ITrackApp.tsx:10909-10942, app-ux-verify/M-401-load.png), and the visibilitychange refetch at :2305 catches many expiries first.
findings.impact: A user who returns to an open tab after session expiry, or hits a Railway HTML 502 mid-deploy, and submits the 20-field activity sheet sees a parser error instead of 'sign in again'; the draft survives in the browser, but the message reads as a broken product at the moment of saving.
findings.recommendation: In runAction, treat response.status === 401 like the loader's authenticationFailure state (same 'Reload and sign in' recovery); guard response.json() behind a content-type check and map non-JSON or 5xx bodies to a fixed 'The server is unavailable — try again in a moment' message with the raw text in a disclosure.

findings.title: No account self-service: display name, email, password and account deletion cannot be changed or requested anywhere in the product
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:9240-9265 (Profile account card: avatar, name, email, Sign out only); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:190 (known routes: signup, login, logout, request-reset, reset, resend); app/api/workspace/route.ts:12377-12459 (no account/user action)
findings.evidence: Profile control dump as a non-demo user (app-ux-new@example.test): Sign out, weeklyGoal x5, Start next Monday, Manage reminders, Add all check-ins to calendar, How to install — nothing else. grep for delete-account|deleteUser|deleteAccount|change-password|changePassword|change-email|updateDisplayName|updateProfile across auth-routes.mjs, auth.mjs, route.ts and ITrackApp.tsx returns nothing. The only password path is the public /reset email-link flow; the display name is fixed at signup. The finder mentioned this only inside 02's recommendation, not as a finding.
findings.impact: A public self-serve product holding professional license records offers no way to delete the account, correct a mistyped name, change the email, or rotate a password from inside the app — a visible trust gap on the settings page and a likely privacy-law exposure (deletion requests) at launch.
findings.recommendation: Add an Account section to Profile: edit display name; change email with re-verification; change password (POST /auth/change-password requiring the current password); Delete account with typed confirmation that cascades workspace rows, evidence files and sessions. Land it alongside the sign-out fix in app-ux-02.

findings.title: Self-serve funnel dead-ends in prod: no verification email, bouncing support address, no contact link, and unverified accounts purged after 7 days
findings.location: deploy/railway/email.mjs:5; deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:223; deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:69; deploy/railway/auth.mjs:15,176,242-243; deploy/railway/serve.mjs:194,236-237,252; deploy/railway/pages/landing.html:141; DNS itrackceu.com
findings.evidence: email.mjs:5 returns {error:'email-not-configured'} when RESEND_API_KEY/AUTH_EMAIL_FROM are unset (serve.mjs:236-237; the task brief and memory both confirm they are unset in prod). auth-routes.mjs:223 then redirects to /signup?sent=1&mail=down, which renders signup.html:69: 'Your account was created, but the verification email could not be sent. Contact us and we'll activate you manually.' with no link, address or button (screenshot signup-mail-down-desktop-light.png). Login refuses the account (auth.mjs:176 'unverified'); password reset also requires verified_at IS NOT NULL (auth.mjs:219); the login page's resend path fails silently (see landing-auth-06). auth.mjs:242-243 deletes users WHERE verified_at IS NULL AND created_at older than UNVERIFIED_TTL_MS = 7 days, run by fireCron every 15 min (serve.mjs:194,252). The only contact channel, mailto:support@itrackceu.com (landing.html:141), cannot receive mail: dig @8.8.8.8 itrackceu.com MX -> NOERROR, 0 answers; no TXT/SPF; _dmarc and resend._domainkey NXDOMAIN; RFC 5321 A-record fallback 69.46.46.121:25 is closed (nc -w3 failed). There is no admin/manual-activation route in the gateway, and the '[auth] verification link' log lines are the only recovery path. Railway HTTP logs for the current deployment (b8b32146, live since 2026-08-12 12:24 UTC, commit 3f477e6) contain no POST /auth/signup or /auth/login at all (58-request sample, only audit probes) — no evidence any stranger has ever completed the funnel.
findings.impact: 100% of strangers who sign up are stranded: account created, cannot verify, cannot log in, cannot reset, promised manual activation is not operationally possible, and their record is silently deleted a week later. Every marketing dollar or SEO gain aimed at itrackceu.com currently converts to zero.
findings.recommendation: Before any traffic: (1) verify itrackceu.com in Resend and publish its DKIM/SPF (TXT) + DMARC records at Name.com, set RESEND_API_KEY and AUTH_EMAIL_FROM='iTrack <no-reply@itrackceu.com>'; (2) give support@itrackceu.com an MX (Name.com forwarding to Gmail) and add a reply-to on auth mail; (3) make the mail-down flash a real escape hatch: mailto link with subject prefilled, plus 'try again' (POST /auth/resend); (4) consider letting unverified users log in with a persistent 'verify your email to enable reminders' banner so the funnel never hard-blocks on deliverability; (5) alert on any email-not-configured/send-failed result (log level error + health endpoint field); (6) suspend the 7-day purge while email is down, or extend it to 30 days.
findings.verifier_note: Verified live, not from memory: Railway prod variables (service itrack, env production) contain no RESEND_API_KEY or AUTH_EMAIL_FROM, so email.mjs:5 returns email-not-configured and auth-routes.mjs:223 redirects to /signup?sent=1&mail=down. Rendered that state (signup-mail-down-desktop-light.png): flash text 'Contact us and we'll activate you manually' with zero links/buttons inside it; page links are only '/', '/login'. dig @8.8.8.8: itrackceu.com MX empty, TXT empty, _dmarc and resend._domainkey NXDOMAIN, 69.46.46.121:25 closed (dns.txt) — support@itrackceu.com cannot receive. auth.mjs:242 purge confirmed and PROVEN to run: deploy log 2026-08-19T04:25Z '[auth] cleaned up 1 stale unverified account(s)' (exactly 7 days after launch). Railway HTTP logs, 30-day window: ~50 GET /signup 200 but zero POST /auth/signup and zero POST /auth/login (only today's audit GET 404 probes); last 200 POSTs are all WordPress/xmlrpc scans. Nuances: PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unset but RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN=itrackceu.com, so links would be correct once mail works; the '[auth] verification link' log fallback exists and Railway auth now works (whoami OK), but there is nothing to activate and no user-facing path. P1 stands.

findings.title: No working sign-out on the website: the only Sign out control links to a 404 route from the old hosting platform
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:9258-9263 (href="/signout-with-chatgpt?return_to=%2F"); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:234-239 (POST /auth/logout, unused); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:6 and deploy/railway/auth.mjs:14,195-209 (30-day sliding session)
findings.evidence: grep of app/, db/ and vite.config.ts finds no handler for /signout-with-chatgpt; GET http://localhost:3000/signout-with-chatgpt?return_to=%2F on the dev server returns 404 text/plain; the gateway proxies any authenticated non-page path straight to the worker, so prod behaves the same. The gateway's real logout is POST /auth/logout (auth-routes.mjs:234-239) and nothing in the client calls it (grep 'logout' in app/ returns only the ChatGPT href). Sessions are Max-Age 30 days and sessionUser() extends expiry on every request, so an abandoned session never expires while the tab is used. (Not exercised on prod with a live session per the no-login rule; verified on dev + by code.)
findings.impact: A user on a shared or public computer cannot end their session; the only way out is clearing site cookies. For a product that stores license numbers and certificate images, that is a security and trust defect in a core account flow.
findings.recommendation: Replace the anchor with a same-origin form: <form method="post" action="/auth/logout"><button>Sign out</button></form> (the Origin/Referer CSRF check passes). Also make the gateway answer GET /auth/logout with a 303 to / (or a confirm page) so stale links degrade gracefully, and after logout land on the landing page with a 'Signed out' note. Keep this control when the Profile screen is redesigned.
findings.verifier_note: Reproduced: grep of app/, db/, vite.config.ts finds the only sign-out control at app/ITrackApp.tsx:9258-9263 (Sign out; public/sw.js:24 merely lists the path). GET http://localhost:3000/signout-with-chatgpt?return_to=%2F -> 404 text/plain 'Not Found'. Gateway has POST /auth/logout (auth-routes.mjs:234-239) and nothing calls it; GET https://itrackceu.com/auth/logout -> 404 live (non-POST /auth/* is 404 at auth-routes.mjs:191). On dev the demo user shows 'Local preview' instead of the button, so the anchor was verified by code + direct GET rather than by click. One correction to the evidence: the session is NOT indefinitely sliding from the browser's side — the cookie carries a fixed Max-Age=30d and is never re-issued (see landing-auth-M-03) — but that does not change the finding: a user has no way to end a session for up to 30 days except clearing cookies. Core account flow broken on the only product: P1 stands.

findings.title: UA/Accept gating for the retired iOS shell serves 401 Basic to Google tooling, every social/link-preview bot, AI crawlers, SEO tools, uptime monitors and HEAD requests
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:190-217 (wantsHtml at 190, isBrowser at 201, landing at 203, 303 /login at 207, 401 Basic at 212); tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs:98-107 (pins the 401 for the WKWebView UA)
findings.evidence: Live matrix against https://itrackceu.com/ (headers saved as ua-*.headers / ua2-*.headers). 200 landing: Googlebot desktop, Googlebot smartphone, bingbot (Chrome-style UA), Applebot, PetalBot, Chrome-Lighthouse, Google-InspectionTool MOBILE, Google-Read-Aloud, Chrome, Firefox, Safari, iOS Safari. 401 'Authentication required' + WWW-Authenticate: Basic: Googlebot/2.1 legacy UA, Google-InspectionTool DESKTOP (Search Console live test), Google-Site-Verification, GoogleOther, Googlebot-Image, AdsBot-Google, bingbot legacy UA, DuckDuckBot, YandexBot, facebookexternalhit, Twitterbot, LinkedInBot, Slackbot, Discordbot, WhatsApp, iMessage (Facebot), GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, AhrefsBot, SemrushBot, UptimeRobot, curl, python-requests, any client with no Accept header, Safari with Accept: */*, and HEAD / from Safari. Root cause: the landing/303 branch requires GET + Accept containing text/html + a UA containing 'Safari/' or 'Firefox/'; everything else falls through to the Basic challenge that only the Capacitor WKWebView shell needed. Non-HTML browser requests hit the same branch: Chrome's favicon request (Accept: image/*) -> 401, apple-touch-icon -> 401, fetch('/api/workspace') -> 401 Basic (ua2-chrome-fetch-api-json.headers).
findings.impact: No link previews anywhere iTrack is shared (Slack, iMessage, LinkedIn, X, WhatsApp, Discord); Search Console desktop live tests and HTML-tag site verification fail; AI answer engines and SEO tools cannot read the page; uptime monitors report the homepage down; and the product decision to retire the iOS app removes the only reason this gate exists.
findings.recommendation: Remove the isBrowser/Safari heuristic and the Basic-auth fallback for unauthenticated requests: serve landing.html for any unauthenticated GET or HEAD on '/', 303 /login for other HTML navigations, and a plain JSON 401 without WWW-Authenticate for API paths. Keep /api/widget-summary's Bearer path only if the widget survives; otherwise drop ITRACK_USERS/basicIdentity and the fail-closed bootstrap requirement in serve.mjs. Update tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs (98-107, 85-87) and the memory note that says not to simplify this away — that instruction was tied to the TestFlight shell.
findings.verifier_note: Re-ran the UA matrix against https://itrackceu.com/ (prod-matrix.txt): 200 for Safari/Chrome/Firefox, Chrome-style Googlebot, InspectionTool mobile, modern bingbot; 401 text/plain + 'WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="iTrack"' for legacy Googlebot, Google-InspectionTool desktop, Google-Site-Verification, legacy bingbot, facebookexternalhit, Twitterbot, LinkedInBot, Slackbot, Facebot, WhatsApp, Discordbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, AhrefsBot, UptimeRobot, curl, Safari with Accept */* or no Accept, HEAD /, Chrome favicon (image Accept) and fetch /api/workspace (JSON Accept). Root cause matches gateway.mjs:190-215; tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs:98-107 pins the WKWebView 401 and :85-87 the Firefox branch. Added nuance (see M-04): the gate only covers '/', because PAGE_ROUTES at gateway.mjs:175 is evaluated before it — curl, facebookexternalhit and legacy Googlebot all get 200 on /login and /signup. P2 is right: modern Googlebot/bingbot do get the page, so this hurts previews, verification tooling and monitors rather than blocking indexing outright.

findings.title: No crawl/SEO fundamentals: robots.txt, sitemap, favicon, manifest, OG image all redirect to /login; no canonical, OG/Twitter tags, JSON-LD, www host, or HSTS; railway.app host is a duplicate
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:16-20 (PAGE_ROUTES allowlist) and :204-208 (everything else 303 /login); deploy/railway/pages/landing.html:1-8 (head); DNS www.itrackceu.com; https://itrack-production-da8b.up.railway.app/
findings.evidence: With a Safari UA: /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /favicon.ico, /favicon.svg, /apple-touch-icon.png, /manifest.webmanifest, /og.png, /icon-192.png, /.well-known/security.txt, /llms.txt, /privacy, /terms, /about, /help all answer 303 -> /login (path-*.headers); with an image Accept the favicon answers 401. The landing head has only charset, viewport, title (43 chars) and description (142 chars, ends 'Free during beta.'): no <link rel=icon>, no canonical, no og:*/twitter:* tags, no JSON-LD, no theme-color/color-scheme (render-report prod-meta: icons [], canonical null, og [], jsonld 0). The 2400x1260 public/og.png exists and already reads 'iTrack — A clear path to renewal', but is unreachable when logged out and unreferenced by the landing. www.itrackceu.com is NXDOMAIN and the Let's Encrypt cert SAN covers only the apex. The railway.app URL serves a byte-identical landing (diff clean) with no canonical or redirect. No strict-transport-security header on any response. WebSearch for "itrackceu.com" returns no result for the domain four weeks after launch. Auth pages (/login, /signup, /reset, /verify) are indexable with no robots meta; /verify?token=bogus returns 200.
findings.impact: The site cannot be favicon'd, previewed, verified in Search Console by HTML tag, or crawled properly; duplicate-host indexing dilutes what little authority exists; users who type www get a resolution error, which reads as 'site is down'.
findings.recommendation: Add a public static allowlist in the gateway (serve from deploy/railway/pages/static or dist/client): /robots.txt (User-agent: * / Disallow: /api/ /auth/ /verify /reset / Sitemap: https://itrackceu.com/sitemap.xml), /sitemap.xml (/, /signup, /login, future /privacy /terms), /favicon.svg + /favicon.ico + /apple-touch-icon.png, /og.png, /manifest.webmanifest, /.well-known/security.txt. In landing.html add <link rel=canonical href="https://itrackceu.com/">, og:title/description/image/url/type, twitter:card=summary_large_image, theme-color, and JSON-LD (SoftwareApplication/WebApplication, applicationCategory BusinessApplication, offers price 0 USD, plus Organization with the support email). Add <meta name=robots content="noindex,follow"> to login/signup/reset/verify and return 404/410 for bad verify tokens. Create www A/ALIAS at Name.com, add it to the Railway custom domains so the cert covers it, and 301 www + the railway.app host to https://itrackceu.com/ in the gateway. Send HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains) once www is live.
findings.verifier_note: Live with a Safari UA: /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /favicon.ico, /favicon.svg, /apple-touch-icon.png, /manifest.webmanifest, /og.png, /icon-192.png, /.well-known/security.txt, /llms.txt, /privacy, /terms, /about, /help, /support all 303 -> https://itrackceu.com/login; /verify?token=bogus 200. Landing head (render-report.json landing): canonical null, icons [], og/twitter [], jsonld 0, robots meta null, title 43 chars, description ends 'Free during beta.' www.itrackceu.com NXDOMAIN (curl: could not resolve). Cert SAN = itrackceu.com only (Let's Encrypt, exp 2026-11-10). No strict-transport-security on any response; http->https 301 exists at the edge. Duplicate hosts are worse than reported: Railway list_domains shows TWO service domains (itrack-production-da8b and itrack-production-9128) plus the custom domain, and both railway.app hosts return the byte-identical landing (cmp clean). WebSearch for "itrackceu.com" returned no result for the domain. public/og.png is 2400x1260 and unreachable logged out.

findings.title: Verification link is consumed and a session is minted on a bare GET, so mail-security scanners burn the link and the human sees 'invalid, already used, or expired'
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:162-172 (verifyEmail on GET at 164, issueSessionCookie at 166, 303 / at 168); deploy/railway/pages/verify.html:66-70; deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:118-128 (24 h expiry)
findings.evidence: GET /verify?token=… calls store.verifyEmail() (single-use: auth.mjs #consumeToken marks used_at) and immediately issues a 30-day session cookie to whatever client fetched it. Corporate link scanners (Microsoft SafeLinks, Proofpoint, Mimecast, Gmail's prefetch in some setups) GET links before the user clicks; the account then IS verified but the user's click renders verify.html: 'This verification link is invalid, already used, or expired. Log in to request a fresh link — we'll offer to resend it if your account still needs verification.' (verify-error-desktop-light.png). Because the account is now verified, logging in works but nothing tells the user that; the copy actively sends them to look for a resend that will not be offered. The scanner also holds a valid session cookie for the account. The plan's own final-review notes already flagged 'verify link is consumed by GET' as a deferred minor.
findings.impact: A meaningful share of professional users (hospital, government, corporate mailboxes) will hit a confusing failure page at the single most important moment of onboarding, and a third-party service is issued a live session for their account.
findings.recommendation: Render a lightweight confirmation page on GET /verify?token= with a single POST button ('Confirm my email'), and consume the token only on POST — or, at minimum, verify on GET but do not issue a session (redirect to /login?verified=1 with a green 'Email confirmed — log in' flash). Make the failure page say 'If you already confirmed, just log in' and offer the resend form inline with an email field. Consider a 72 h verify TTL.
findings.verifier_note: Code verified at the cited lines: gateway.mjs:163-172 consumes the token on a bare GET (store.verifyEmail -> auth.mjs:105-116 #consumeToken sets used_at, single use) and immediately calls issueSessionCookie for whatever client fetched it, then 303 /. verify.html:66-70 error copy confirmed; rendered on prod (/verify?token=bogus -> 200, h1 'Verification link problem', prod-verify-bogus-mobile-dark.png). The scanner scenario itself cannot be reproduced without a mailbox, but the mechanism is exact and the project's own memory note lists 'verify link is consumed by GET (mail scanners can burn it)' as a known deferred item. The 24h TTL is auth.mjs:12. P2 stands (moot in practice until email works, then immediately live).

findings.title: 'Resend the link' on the unverified-login error posts an empty email (form values lost on redirect; hidden field only fills on a typed input event) and then reports success
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/login.html:72-78 (flash with nested form, hidden #resend-email at 75) and :98-100 (input listener); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:258-264 (resend branch; limiter at 259, unconditional /login?resent=1 at 264; auth.mjs:158-167 newVerifyToken)
findings.evidence: Playwright check on login.html?error=unverified (render-report login-unverified-resend-*): the email field is empty after the server redirect, FormData of the resend form has email='' , a programmatic value set (what password managers/autofill do) still yields '', and only a typed input populates it. Server side newVerifyToken('') returns null and the route still redirects to /login?resent=1, which shows 'If that account needs verification, a fresh link is on its way.' — a false success. The resend button is an inline <button> inside a <div class=flash> nested inside the login card, rendered 99x16 px (login-unverified-mobile-light.png), with a stray space before the period ('resend the link .'). The resend route also shares the password-reset limiter bucket reset:${ip} (3/hour) while its error copy says 'Wait a few minutes and try again' (login.html:60).
findings.impact: The one recovery path for unverified users silently does nothing for anyone who clicks it before retyping their address — which is everyone, because the redirect emptied the field — while telling them a link is coming.
findings.recommendation: Carry the email through the redirect (/login?error=unverified&email=… or a short-lived signed cookie) and prefill both the visible field and the hidden one; make resend a proper form with its own visible email input and a 44 px button; return an honest neutral message ('If that address has an unverified account, we sent a new link'); give resend its own limiter and matching copy. Fix the copy spacing. Add role=alert to the flash (see landing-auth-11).
findings.verifier_note: Reproduced with Playwright on file://login.html?error=unverified (render-report.json resend; login-unverified-mobile-light.png): flash visible, email field '', FormData(resend form).get('email') === '' initially AND after a programmatic value set (autofill path); populated only after a typed input event (login.html:98-100). Button measures 98.8x16 px, no role/aria-live, and innerText reads 'resend the link .' with the stray space. Server side: auth-routes.mjs:258-264 shares resetLimiter ('reset:'+ip, 3/h) and redirects to /login?resent=1 unconditionally; auth.mjs:155-159 newVerifyToken('') returns null, so the success flash ('a fresh link is on its way') is false. Copy mismatch confirmed: login.html:71 says 'Wait a few minutes' for a 1-hour bucket. P2 stands.

findings.title: Expired or logged-out app tabs get 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Basic on every fetch, triggering the browser's native HTTP-auth dialog before the app's own 'Reload and sign in' state
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:210-216; app/ITrackApp.tsx:1929-1937 (fetch /api/workspace) and :10896-10940 (WorkspaceLoadFailure, authenticationFailure at 10906)
findings.evidence: curl https://itrackceu.com/api/workspace with a Chrome UA and Accept: application/json -> HTTP 401, content-type text/plain, WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="iTrack" (ua2-chrome-fetch-api-json.headers). In the Playwright prod render, a same-origin fetch('/favicon.ico') from the landing page never resolved and was cut off by an 8 s race (render-report prod-favicon-fetch-from-page: hung=true), consistent with a pending credential challenge; the first run of the script hung on the same call for eight minutes. Same-origin fetch/XHR 401s with a Basic challenge raise the native 'Sign in to itrackceu.com' dialog in Chrome, Firefox and Safari. Sessions expire after 30 days idle, and resetPassword() deletes all sessions (auth.mjs:229-237), so an open tab on another device will hit this path. The client's own recovery UI ('Your sign-in needs to be refreshed… Reload and sign in') is correct but only appears after the JSON parse of a text/plain body throws.
findings.impact: An off-brand, phishing-looking system credential prompt appears in the app at exactly the moment a user's session lapses; users who type their password into it are silently logged in via the Basic path with no session cookie, and the prompt returns on the next request.
findings.recommendation: Once the iOS shell is gone, never send WWW-Authenticate: Basic. For unauthenticated non-HTML requests return 401 application/json {"error":"unauthenticated","login":"/login"}; for HTML navigations 303 /login?next=<path>. In the client, on 401 navigate to /login?next=… instead of showing the reload card. Delete basicIdentity/basicCache/basicFailLimiter and the ITRACK_USERS bootstrap once the widget feed is retired or moved to a bearer token only.
findings.verifier_note: Live: curl https://itrackceu.com/api/workspace with Chrome UA + Accept: application/json -> 401, content-type text/plain, WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="iTrack", charset="UTF-8" (gateway.mjs:211-215). Playwright prod run from the landing page (HeadlessChrome/152): both fetch('/api/workspace', {accept: application/json}) and fetch('/favicon.ico') never resolved and were cut off by my 8 s race (render-report.json prodFetch: hung=true for both) — the headless signature of a pending credential challenge; in headed Chrome/Firefox/Safari a same-origin fetch 401 with a Basic challenge raises the native login prompt (only cross-origin subresource prompts are blocked). Client path confirmed: ITrackApp.tsx:1935-1940 parses JSON and 10896-10940 shows 'Reload and sign in' only after that throws. Basic path accepting DB accounts by email confirmed at gateway.mjs:72-92 and resetPassword deleting sessions at auth.mjs:234. See M-03: this prompt is guaranteed for every user 30 days after login, not just an edge case. P2 stands.

findings.title: Landing and signup still sell 'Free during beta', an ad-supported Free tier and a $9.99/mo 'Pro coming soon' tier — copy that must be removed, and tests pin it
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/landing.html:7 (meta description), :95 (badge), :111-138 (pricing section), :141 (footer); deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:67; tests/auth-pages.test.mjs:23-32; tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs:79

On time. | iTrack keeps your professional licenses, certifications, and CE hours in one place — and reminds you before anything lapses. | Create your free account | I already have one | [📅] Renewal deadlines — See every expiration date at a glance, with how much runway you have left on each credential. | [🎓] CE progress — Track continuing-education hours against each credential's requirement, cycle by cycle. | [🔔] Push reminders — Get nudged before deadlines on your phone and desktop — not after they've passed. | [🗂️] Evidence vault — Keep certificates and proof of completion beside each credential, and export everything when an auditor asks. | Simple pricing — Everything is free while iTrack is in beta. | Free $0 ad-supported: Unlimited credentials; Renewal & CE reminders; Evidence vault and export — Sign up free | Pro COMING SOON $9.99/mo or $79/yr: Everything in Free; No ads; Priority support — Start free today | iTrack is in beta — free while we build.
