'ad-supported' and 'No ads' promise an ad model that is now cancelled; 'beta' implies impermanence and a future price.
findings.impact: Visitors are told the free product is temporary, ad-funded and about to cost $9.99/month — the opposite of the decided positioning — which suppresses signups and will read as a bait-and-switch later; the pinned tests turn a copy change into a red CI run.
findings.recommendation: Immediately: delete the pricing section, the badge, the beta footer sentence, the signup subtitle and the description tail; replace with one honest line ('Free to use. No ads, no card, no tiers.') and a 'Contact' link; update the four test assertions to assert the absence of $, 'beta' and 'ad-supported'. Keep 'No card required' — it converts. Do this before the redesign rather than as part of it.
findings.verifier_note: Copy verified in deploy/railway/pages/landing.html:7 (description), :95 (badge), :111-138 (pricing: 'Free $0 ad-supported', 'Pro coming soon $9.99/mo or $79/yr', 'No ads'), :141 (footer 'in beta — free while we build'), signup.html:67 ('Free during beta. No card required.'); prod landing is byte-identical to the repo file (cmp). Screenshots landing-desktop-light.png / prod-landing-mobile-dark.png show the badge and both tiers. Pins verified by reading: tests/auth-pages.test.mjs:25-28 assert /Free during beta/, /\$9\.99\/mo/, /\$79\/yr/, /coming soon/i; tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs:79 asserts /Free during beta/ on the served landing. Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-itrack-public-signup-design.md:138-144 shows this was the Phase-2 monetization plan now cancelled. P2 / fix_regardless stands.

findings.title: Landing fails the 10-second test on who it is for and why to trust it: no professions/states, no source-linked-rules or organizer-not-authority boundary, no privacy line, no screenshot, no 'what happens after signup'
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/landing.html:92-108 (hero + features); README.md:41-58 (the claims that exist but are not on the page); deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:65-67
findings.evidence: The hero communicates WHAT (licenses, certifications, CE hours + reminders) but nothing about WHO: the words profession, state, board, nurse, CPA, counselor, CRC, etc. never appear, although the catalog holds 170 source-linked templates across 53 profession labels and 98 issuing bodies, 79 of them state-specific (CA, FL, NJ, NY, PA, TX) per README.md:41-45. No trust block: nothing about source links with review dates, the 'organizer, not an issuing authority' boundary (README.md:53-58), private evidence storage, on-device certificate scanning, export, or account deletion. No product image (the spec explicitly deferred screenshots: 'no asset pipeline in the proxy'), no FAQ, no 'how it works', no author/about, no social proof. Feature icons are emoji (📅🎓🔔🗂️), which render differently per OS. 'Push reminders… on your phone and desktop' now depends on web push, which on iOS requires Add-to-Home-Screen — unexplained. Signup gives no preview of the next step (a verification email), and the sent-state copy is the only place the 24 h link expiry is mentioned. Heading outline: h1 -> four h3s -> h2 'Simple pricing' (axe heading-order). Word count 165; docH 1376 px desktop / 2278 px mobile; primary CTA is above the fold on both (mobile CTA top 382 px of 844).
findings.impact: A licensed professional cannot tell within ten seconds whether their credential or state is covered or whether their records are safe here, and a self-serve product with no trust signals converts poorly and earns no search or AI-answer visibility.
findings.recommendation: The redesigned landing must include, in order: (1) outcome headline + one-sentence definition naming licenses, certifications and CE; (2) a who-for strip with profession/state chips drawn from the catalog (nursing, counseling/CRC, CPA, securities, safety, dental… + CA/FL/NJ/NY/PA/TX) and a 'not listed? build a custom credential' line; (3) a real product screenshot or an instrument-panel-style mock of the Home view; (4) how it works in three steps mirroring the in-app onboarding (choose template + state → confirm cycle dates → log learning as you go); (5) a trust block: source-linked rules with review dates, 'iTrack is an organizer, not an issuing authority — your board's current instructions control', private evidence vault, export/delete anytime, free with no ads; (6) FAQ (Is it free? Which professions? What if my board isn't listed? What happens after I sign up? Can I export?); (7) footer with Privacy, Terms, Contact, About. Expose a public read-only catalog summary (profession/state counts) from the gateway so the numbers stay true automatically.
findings.verifier_note: Measured on the rendered landing (render-report.json landing/landingMobileFold): 165 words; words 'state', 'board', 'nurse', 'CPA', 'counsel', 'privacy', 'terms' absent ('profession' matches only via 'professional licenses'); footer links = [mailto:support@itrackceu.com]; heading outline H1 -> 4x H3 -> H2 'Simple pricing' -> 2x H3; 0 <main>; docHeight 1376 desktop / 2278 mobile; mobile primary CTA top 382 px of 844 (above the fold, as the finder said). README.md:41-58 claims checked verbatim (170 templates, 53 profession labels, 98 issuing bodies, 79 state-specific across CA/FL/NJ/NY/PA/TX; 'organizer, not an issuing authority'). Spec line 145 confirms 'No screenshots at launch (no asset pipeline in the proxy)'. Web push exists in the client (4 pushManager refs), so the claim is true on the web but the iOS add-to-home-screen caveat is unexplained. Emoji glyphs confirmed at landing.html:105-108. P2 / carry_into_redesign stands.

findings.title: No privacy policy, terms of service, or consent language anywhere in the public funnel
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:65-84; deploy/railway/pages/landing.html:140-142; deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:16-20 (PAGE_ROUTES has no /privacy or /terms)
findings.evidence: GET /privacy, /terms, /about, /help, /support each 303 -> /login (path-privacy.headers etc.). The signup form has no 'By creating an account you agree…' line and no link near the submit button; the landing footer contains only a mailto. The product stores license identifiers, certificate images/PDFs and email addresses, and the auth store purges unverified accounts after 7 days (auth.mjs:242) — a retention behaviour users are never told about. The Phase-2 spec deferred 'consent/privacy compliance' to the ads/billing phase, which is now cancelled, so nothing owns it.
findings.impact: Licensed professionals (and any EU/UK/CA visitor) have no basis to trust the site with regulated-career data; missing policies also block Search Console/AI-crawler trust signals, Resend/Google sender requirements, and expose the operator legally.
findings.recommendation: Add /privacy and /terms as self-contained public pages (register in PAGE_ROUTES and the sitemap), covering: what is collected, where it lives (Cloudflare D1/R2 state on a Railway volume, US), retention (unverified accounts deleted after 7 days; user-initiated deletion), no ads/no sale of data, transactional email only, contact address. Link them in the footer of every public page and directly under the signup button ('By creating an account you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy'). Add an account-deletion path in the app to make the policy true.
findings.verifier_note: Live: /privacy, /terms, /about, /help, /support -> 303 /login (prod-matrix.txt); PAGE_ROUTES at gateway.mjs:16-20 has only /signup, /login, /reset. Rendered signup: consentText false (no 'agree/terms/privacy' anywhere on the page), footer of landing has only the mailto. No delete-account path exists in the client or worker (grep 'delete account|privacy policy|terms of service' in app/ITrackApp.tsx and app/api/workspace/route.ts returns nothing). The 7-day purge (auth.mjs:15,242) is disclosed nowhere. P2 stands.

findings.title: Every CTA fails WCAG AA contrast; flashes are not announced; pages ignore dark mode while the app supports it
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/*.html shared <style> block (tokens --accent #007aff, --paper #f2f2f7, --amber #b97706/--amber-soft #fff0d0; .flash; .note 13px links); landing.html:92-140
findings.evidence: axe (wcag2a/2aa/21aa + best-practice) on all five pages at 1440 and 390: color-contrast [serious] on every page — primary buttons white on #007aff = 4.02:1, quiet links #007aff on #f2f2f7 = 3.60:1, badge #b97706 on #fff0d0 = 3.27:1 (computed); link-in-text-block [serious] on landing/signup (links distinguished by colour only); heading-order and landmark-one-main [moderate] on landing. Zero aria-live/role=alert/role=status across the five pages (grep count 0), so screen readers never announce 'That email and password don't match' etc.; errors are not tied to fields (no aria-describedby/aria-invalid; render-report inputs). Signup shows no password rule before submit (hintTextVisibleBeforeSubmit=false; only the browser's 'Please lengthen this text to 10 characters' after a failed submit). Tap targets: 'Forgot your password?', 'Create an account', 'Back to login', 'Get in touch' and 'resend the link' are 16 px tall. Dark mode: with prefers-color-scheme dark the body stays rgb(242,242,247) and cards white on all pages (landing-desktop-dark.png, prod-landing-mobile-dark-fold.png); no color-scheme or theme-color meta — while app/globals.css:374 and layout.tsx define a full dark theme, so a night-time visitor goes bright-white landing → dark app.
findings.impact: The conversion path is harder to read for low-vision users and legally weaker under ADA/508 expectations for a professional-licensing tool; screen-reader users get no feedback on failed logins; the light-only pages make the first transition into the product feel like two different sites.
findings.recommendation: Acceptance criteria for the redesigned public pages: accent colour ≥4.5:1 on paper and card (or dark text on light accent buttons), underlined in-text links, role="alert" on error flashes and role="status" on success flashes, aria-describedby hint + error text per field, ≥24 px (ideally 44 px) interactive targets, a visible 'At least 10 characters' hint before typing, an h2 above the feature cards, a <main> landmark, and prefers-color-scheme support using the same tokens as the app (plus theme-color/color-scheme meta).
findings.verifier_note: Re-ran axe (wcag2a/2aa/21aa/best-practice) on all five pages at 1440x900 and 390x844 (render-report.json axe): color-contrast [serious] on every page — white on #007aff = 4.01:1 (15px, expected 4.5), #007aff on #f2f2f7 = 3.59:1, badge #b97706 on #fff0d0 = 3.26:1, 13px #007aff note links on white = 4.01:1; link-in-text-block [serious] on landing and signup; heading-order + landmark-one-main [moderate] on landing. grep: 0 aria-live / role=alert / role=status and 0 prefers-color-scheme across the five files; rendered forms have 0 aria-describedby / aria-invalid, no hint before submit, no autofocus. Tap targets measured on mobile: 'Forgot your password?' 138x16, 'Create an account' 111x16, 'Log in' 37x16, 'Back to login' 78x16 (one correction: 'Get in touch' wraps and measures 189x36, not 16 px). Dark mode: with colorScheme dark, body stays rgb(242,242,247) and cards rgb(255,255,255) on all five pages; no color-scheme/theme-color meta (landing-desktop-dark.png, prod-landing-mobile-dark.png), while app/globals.css:374 and layout.tsx:82-84 define a dark theme. P2 stands.

findings.title: Login → app hand-off gaps: no return-to for deep links, auth pages shown to logged-in users, no 'verified' acknowledgement, HEAD requests rejected
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:175-178 (PAGE_ROUTES served before the session check at 180), :204-208 (303 /login without next), :190 (HEAD excluded); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:231 (login always redirects to /); app/ITrackApp.tsx:6897-6960 (first-run hero)
findings.evidence: GET /credentials logged out -> 303 /login with no next parameter; after login the route always redirects to / (auth-routes.mjs:231), so bookmarks and reminder links land on Home. /login and /signup are served before the session cookie is checked (gateway.mjs:175 vs 180), so a logged-in user sees the login form and logging in again mints a second session row. After GET /verify succeeds the user is 303'd to / with no flag; the app shows the generic 'Welcome, {first name}' onboarding hero with nothing saying the email was confirmed. HEAD / with a Safari UA -> 401 (curl -I), so link checkers and some monitors fail. /login?next=… is silently ignored (200, unused).
findings.impact: Small but repeated friction at the seam between marketing and product: lost deep links, duplicate sessions, and a missed moment to confirm success and set expectations.
findings.recommendation: Add a same-origin-only next parameter (validate: starts with '/', not '//'), carried through /login and honoured by /auth/login and /verify; redirect authenticated users from /login and /signup to /; redirect to /?verified=1 after verification and have the app show a one-time 'Email confirmed' toast; treat HEAD like GET for the landing and public pages.
findings.verifier_note: Live: GET /credentials logged out -> 303 https://itrackceu.com/login with no next parameter; /login?next=%2Fcredentials -> 200 and the parameter is unused; HEAD / and HEAD /login with a Safari UA -> 401 (gateway.mjs:190 and :175 both require GET). Code: auth-routes.mjs:231 always redirects to '/'; gateway.mjs:175-178 serves /login and /signup before the session lookup at :180, so a logged-in user can log in again and create a second sessions row (createSession inserts unconditionally, auth.mjs:183-192); /verify success 303 '/' with no flag (gateway.mjs:167) and the first-run hero at ITrackApp.tsx:6897-6905 is the generic 'Welcome, {first name}'. P3 stands.

findings.title: Form UX polish: generic server error that wipes all fields, no password guidance or show-password, 'Name' label ambiguous, no autofocus
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:71-80 (form) and :70 (flash-invalid); deploy/railway/pages/login.html:80-86; deploy/railway/pages/reset.html:86-97; deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:214-217
findings.evidence: Server-side validation redirects to /signup?error=invalid with 'Please use a valid email, a display name, and a password of at least 10 characters.' and every field empty (signup-invalid-desktop-light.png) — the user must retype all three to learn which one failed. Password fields have minlength=10 but no visible rule until the browser's native bubble; no show/hide toggle; no maximum guidance. The 'Name' field is used as the display name shown as 'Welcome, {firstName}' in the app, but the label does not say so. No autofocus on the first field on any page; email inputs rely on type=email only (fine) but lack autocapitalize=none for older mobile browsers. autocomplete attributes are correct (name/email/new-password/current-password) — keep them. Rate-limit copy matches the code for signup (5/h), login (10/15 min) and reset (3/h). The signup 'email already has an account' message enumerates accounts, an accepted spec trade-off, while reset is enumeration-safe — inconsistent but defensible.
findings.impact: Each item costs a slice of signups at the form step; together they make the form feel less trustworthy than the backend actually is.
findings.recommendation: Keep values on validation failure (redirect with the fields, or validate client-side first and mark the offending field), show the password rule under the field with aria-describedby, add a show-password toggle, relabel 'Name' as 'Display name (what we call you)', autofocus the first field, and keep the existing autocomplete attributes in the redesign. Consider a strength hint rather than a stricter rule.
findings.verifier_note: Rendered signup.html?error=invalid: flash text matches, name/email/password values all '' (auth-routes.mjs:213 redirects with nothing carried), no hint before submit, no autofocus, 0 aria-describedby / aria-invalid, no show-password control on any page; minlength=10 only (signup.html:79, reset.html:85). Rate-limit copy vs code re-checked: signup 5/h ('Try again in an hour' signup.html:72), login 10/15 min ('Wait a few minutes' login.html:71), reset 3/h ('Try again in an hour' reset.html:70) — consistent. 'Name' feeds firstName(workspace.user.displayName) in the app (ITrackApp.tsx:6902). Email-taken enumeration at signup.html:70 vs enumeration-safe reset at reset.html:69 confirmed. One disagreement: these are acceptance criteria for the redesigned forms (keep autocomplete, add hints/aria/persisted values), so 'carry_into_redesign' fits better than 'moot_once_redesigned'.

findings.title: Three different brand voices: iOS-blue landing wordmark vs. warm green editorial og.png/icon vs. app metadata taglines
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/landing.html:88-91 (wordmark) and :6-7 (title/description); public/og.png; public/icon-192.png / icon-512.png; app/layout.tsx:16-19 (title 'iTrack — A clear path to renewal', different description); app/manifest.ts:6-9 ('iTrack — CE & Renewal Tracker')
findings.evidence: Landing: system-font 'iTrack' with a #007aff 'Track', iOS neutral+blue tokens, title 'iTrack — credential and CE renewal tracking'. public/og.png (2400x1260): cream background, forest-green serif 'A clear path to renewal.', subline 'Credits, evidence, deadlines, and renewal steps — watched for you.', mint app-icon glyph. public/icon-192.png: green arch with a winding path and star — a different mark again. layout.tsx title 'iTrack — A clear path to renewal' with description 'A calm continuing-education companion…'; manifest name 'iTrack — CE & Renewal Tracker' with a third description. (The memory note that og.png still says 'Vigilo' is stale — it reads iTrack.)
findings.impact: Link previews (once they work), the installed icon, the browser tab and the landing page will not look like the same product, weakening recognition and trust at the first three touchpoints.
findings.recommendation: Pick one tagline and description now and use them in landing.html, layout.tsx and manifest.ts (the og.png line 'A clear path to renewal' already matches the warm-editorial direction of the redesign and is a good candidate); make the og.png palette and the icon mark the seed of the redesign's brand tokens so the landing, previews and app icon converge.
findings.verifier_note: Viewed the assets: public/og.png (2400x1260) is cream background, forest-green serif 'A clear path to renewal.', subline 'Credits, evidence, deadlines, and renewal steps — watched for you.', mint 'i' glyph; public/icon-192.png is a green arch with a winding path and a star — neither shares anything with the landing's system-font 'iTrack' wordmark in #007aff (landing.html:87). Three descriptions/taglines confirmed: landing.html:6-7 ('iTrack — credential and CE renewal tracking'), app/layout.tsx:17-19 ('iTrack — A clear path to renewal' / 'A calm continuing-education companion…'), app/manifest.ts:6-9 ('iTrack — CE & Renewal Tracker' / 'Track continuing-education credits, documents, deadlines, and renewal steps.'). The memory note claiming og.png still says Vigilo is indeed stale. P3 stands.

findings.title: Public pages send no security headers (no HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, referrer-policy, CSP); login and reset forms are framable
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:44-55 (servePage writes only content-type and cache-control); Railway edge (301 http→https present, no HSTS)
findings.evidence: Response headers for / , /login, /signup, /reset, /verify: cache-control: no-store, content-type, server, x-railway-* only (prod-root-safari.headers, path-login.headers). No strict-transport-security, x-content-type-options, x-frame-options / CSP frame-ancestors, referrer-policy, or content-security-policy. The reset token travels in the URL (/reset?token=…) and is copied into a hidden field — acceptable, but without a referrer policy any future external link or asset on that page would leak it. Pages inline all CSS/JS (a strict CSP is easy). The rate limiters are in-memory per process and reset on each deploy (auth-routes.mjs:12-37).
findings.impact: Auth forms can be embedded in a third-party frame (clickjacking of login/reset), first-visit downgrade attacks remain possible without HSTS, and the absence of standard headers is visible to any security-conscious evaluator (and to Lighthouse best-practice scores).
findings.recommendation: In servePage() add: strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains (after www exists), x-content-type-options: nosniff, referrer-policy: no-referrer (auth pages) / strict-origin-when-cross-origin (landing), content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'. Move inline scripts to a hashed <script> or nonce when the pages are rebuilt.
findings.verifier_note: Live response headers on /, /login (prod-matrix.txt): only cache-control: no-store, content-type, date, server: railway-hikari, x-railway-request-id, x-railway-edge, x-hikari-trace — no strict-transport-security, x-content-type-options, x-frame-options, content-security-policy, or referrer-policy; matches servePage at gateway.mjs:45-54 writing two headers. http://itrackceu.com/ -> 301 https at the edge (so only HSTS is missing for downgrade protection). reset.html:94-99 copies the URL token into the hidden field; all links on that page are same-origin, so leakage is only a future risk. Rate limiters are in-process Maps (auth-routes.mjs:12-37). P3 stands; frame-ancestors/XFO is the one item worth doing before any redesign work since it is a one-line change.

findings.title: Display name is interpolated unrestricted into the first line of verification and reset emails — the signup form becomes a phishing/spam relay from no-reply@itrackceu.com the moment Resend is enabled
findings.location: deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:118-127 (verificationEmail: greeting = `Hi ${name},`), :129-138 (resetEmail, same pattern), :208 and :212 (name only trimmed and length-checked 1-80; any characters incl. URLs, phone numbers, %0A newlines); limiter :141 (5 signups/hour/IP), :259 (resend 3/hour/IP)
findings.evidence: Read the code paths: the text body starts with the raw name (only the HTML variant is escaped, which does not stop content injection). Nothing else constrains the name; the subject is fixed but the first visible line is attacker-controlled. An attacker can enter any victim's email with name 'URGENT: your license is suspended — call 555-0100' and the victim receives that line from iTrack's own sender, with a real iTrack link beneath it.
findings.impact: Once landing-auth-01 is fixed this is live on day one: it lets strangers send branded mail to arbitrary addresses (5/hour/IP, unlimited IPs) and it is exactly the pattern that gets a brand-new sending domain flagged — undermining the deliverability the launch depends on.
findings.recommendation: Do not echo user input on the first line: greet with 'Hi,' (or the address), or restrict display names used in mail to letters/spaces/apostrophes/hyphens and <=40 chars; keep the full name for the app only. Add this to the email-configuration checklist in landing-auth-01.

findings.title: Re-signup with an email that already has an unverified account is refused for up to 7 days ('already has an account') instead of re-issuing the verification link
findings.location: deploy/railway/auth.mjs:127-143 (createUser: UNIQUE violation -> AuthError email-taken regardless of verified_at); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:215-221 (-> /signup?error=email-taken); deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:70 ('That email already has an account. Log in instead.')
findings.evidence: Code path traced: the users table UNIQUE(email) throws before verified_at is consulted, so an unverified row blocks a fresh attempt until the 7-day purge (auth.mjs:242). The user is then sent to /login, which answers 'hasn't been verified yet' (auth.mjs:176), whose only resend control is the broken one in landing-auth-06.
findings.impact: The natural retry after a lost verification email ('just sign up again') is a dead end for a week; combined with 01/06 there is no working exit from the loop, and the copy ('Log in instead') is misleading for an account that cannot log in.
findings.recommendation: On signup for an existing UNVERIFIED email: replace the password hash, issue a fresh verify token, send it, and show the same neutral 'check your email' state (enumeration-neutral and self-healing). Keep 'email-taken' only for verified accounts.

findings.title: The 'sliding' 30-day session only slides in the database — the cookie has a fixed Max-Age and is never re-issued, so every user is hard-logged-out 30 days after login and lands on the Basic-auth prompt path
findings.location: deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:6 and :106-108 (Max-Age=2592000 fixed at issue time), :145-151 (userForRequest never sets a cookie), :153-156 (cookie issued only by login/verify); deploy/railway/auth.mjs:205-207 (DB expires_at slides on every request); deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:95-124 (proxy never adds set-cookie)
findings.evidence: Traced every set-cookie: issueSessionCookie is called only from POST /auth/login (:230) and GET /verify (gateway.mjs:166); no request path refreshes it. The browser therefore discards the cookie 30 days after login even for daily users, while the DB row keeps sliding (and lingers up to 30 days beyond the cookie).
findings.impact: The native credential dialog in landing-auth-07 is not an edge case but a scheduled event for every active user on day 30, in whatever tab they have open; the design intent (sliding session) is not actually delivered, and stale sessions rows accumulate.
findings.recommendation: Re-issue the cookie whenever it is older than ~24h (store issued_at in the signed value, or compare against sessions.created_at) or on every authenticated HTML navigation; alternatively make it an honest fixed 30-day session and tell users. Ship with the 07 fix so the day-30 expiry redirects to /login instead of prompting for Basic credentials.

findings.title: The UA gate is asymmetric: /login, /signup, /reset and /verify are served to every client while '/' is 401 — so bots and link-unfurlers that fail the homepage still fetch and can index the auth forms (which carry no noindex)
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:175-178 (PAGE_ROUTES served before any UA/Accept check) versus :190-215 (gate applies only to the fall-through, i.e. '/' and deep paths); deploy/railway/pages/{login,signup,reset,verify}.html (no <meta name=robots>)
findings.evidence: Live probes (prod-extra.txt): GET /login with UA curl/8 -> 200 text/html; GET /signup as facebookexternalhit/1.1 -> 200; GET /signup as legacy 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1)' -> 200; the same clients get 401 on '/'. HEAD /login -> 401.
findings.impact: For every crawler and preview bot in the 401 list of landing-auth-03, the only reachable pages are the login and signup forms, so the site's discoverable entry point is a form rather than the landing — the inverse of the intended indexing, and it makes the missing noindex on auth pages consequential rather than theoretical.
findings.recommendation: Resolved by removing the gate (03) plus robots noindex on the four auth pages (04). As an interim one-line fix, serve landing.html for any unauthenticated GET/HEAD on '/' regardless of UA/Accept.

findings.title: The signup 'sent' state has no resend or wrong-address recovery — the form is hidden and the only links go to /login; the sole resend control is reachable only through a failed login (and is broken per 06)
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:68 (flash-sent copy) and :87-90 (form hidden when ?sent=1); deploy/railway/pages/login.html:72-78 (only resend form on the site); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:258-264 (POST /auth/resend exists but is unused from the signup page)
findings.evidence: Rendered signup.html?sent=1 and ?sent=1&mail=down (render-report.json signupStates; signup-mail-down-desktop-light.png): form display none, page links = ['/', '/login', '/login', '/login'], no address echo, no resend button. The route the page would need already exists server-side.
findings.impact: The most common verification failure (message in spam, delayed, or the user wants to fix the address) has no recovery on the page where the user is actually waiting; they must guess to log in, fail, and then type their email again to reach a resend that posts an empty field.
findings.recommendation: On the sent state show the address used, a 'Resend link' POST button to /auth/resend with the email in a hidden field populated server-side (carry it in the redirect), its own limiter and honest neutral copy, plus 'Wrong address? Start over'. Make this part of the redesigned signup screen's acceptance criteria.

findings.title: Login throttling is per-IP only (no per-account throttle, lockout notice or breached-password check), and the still-live Basic-auth path is a second guessing surface against the same accounts
findings.location: deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:142 (loginLimiter 10/15 min keyed 'login:'+ip) and :226-229; deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:61 (basicFailLimiter 20/15 min per IP), :72-92 (DB accounts authenticate over Basic with email as username), :211-215 (challenge sent on every unauthenticated non-HTML request)
findings.evidence: Code read: both limiters key on the last x-forwarded-for entry only; nothing keys on the target email, nothing records or notifies on repeated failures, and passwords are only checked for length >= 10 (auth-routes.mjs:212). Live: curl to /api/workspace returns the Basic challenge, confirming the Basic path is reachable from any client.
findings.impact: Distributed credential stuffing against a known professional's email gets ~30 guesses per IP per 15 minutes across two endpoints with no lockout or alert — modest risk today, but the product will hold license numbers and certificate images for strangers, and the Basic path only ever existed for the retired iOS shell.
findings.recommendation: Add a per-account limiter (e.g. 20 failures/hour keyed by sha256(email)) with a neutral 'try again later' response and a log line; remove the Basic path and ITRACK_USERS bootstrap with the iOS retirement (03/07); optionally add a k-anonymity breached-password check at signup/reset.

findings.title: No funnel instrumentation anywhere: the public pages carry no measurement and the gateway logs nothing on signup/verify/login success, so a dead funnel is invisible to the team
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/*.html (only flash-toggle scripts, no analytics); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:158-166 (deliver logs only failures), :210-232 (signup/login success emit no log line); deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:163-172 (verify success emits nothing)
findings.evidence: Read all five pages and the auth routes: zero success-path logging and zero client measurement. The only available signal is Railway's HTTP log (path + status), which is how this audit found ~50 GET /signup and 0 POST /auth/signup over 30 days — a month-long dead funnel that nothing surfaced.
findings.impact: With conversion explicitly a launch goal, there is no way to see landing -> signup -> verify -> first-credential drop-off, or to detect the next silent breakage (mail down, resend broken) without a manual log dig.
findings.recommendation: Emit PII-free structured log lines for signup_created, verify_ok, verify_failed, login_ok, resend_sent (counts only), expose them on a small /healthz JSON (last-24h counters + email-configured flag), and add a cookieless, privacy-respecting page-view counter to the public pages in the redesign so the funnel can be read weekly.

findings.title: Pushed credential-detail screen leaves the list screen underneath focusable and readable (not inert)
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:4135-4137 (`screen screen-root` + `screen-under` class); app/globals.css:2491-2500 (.screen-root.screen-under only transforms/dims); route /credentials/:id
findings.evidence: probe3: on /credentials/demo-nj-lcsw-2026-253d00f801f4 the `.screen-root.screen-under` element reports inert=false, aria-hidden=null, visibility=visible, transform translateX(-311px) (desktop) / -101px (mobile). Keyboard tab order (desktop) goes skip-link → 4 nav buttons → Log activity → "Add credential" (x=918, under=true) → credential card button (x=-29, w=1112, under=true) → "Add another credential" (under=true) → only then "Credentials" back button of the detail screen; same three hidden stops on mobile at x=-87. Two H1s are exposed ("Every renewal, one clear place." and "Licensed Clinical Social Worker"). contrast-incomplete.log: the under-screen text renders at 1.0–2.95:1 (h1 1.18, "Add credential" 1.15, "Add another credential" 2.82) yet is still in the accessibility tree. Screenshots: shots/detail-desktop-light.png, shots/detail-mobile-light.png.
findings.impact: Keyboard users tab through three invisible/dimmed controls (one of which opens the Add-credential sheet) before reaching the screen they are looking at, and screen-reader users hear the whole credentials list, including a second level-1 heading, before the detail content. Focus order and reading order contradict the visual state (WCAG 2.4.3, 1.3.2).
findings.recommendation: While a detail is pushed, set `inert` (and aria-hidden="true") on `.screen-under` exactly as Modal already does for its siblings, and move focus to the pushed screen's back control or H1 on push and back to the originating card on pop. If the redesign replaces the iOS push-stack with routed pages this becomes moot, but the attribute is a one-line fix now.
findings.verifier_note: Reproduced with my own Playwright run (v-a11y-a.mjs, verify-a.log, 01-detail-desktop.png / 01-detail-mobile.png). On /credentials/demo-nj-lcsw-2026-253d00f801f4 the .screen-root.screen-under element reports inert=false, aria-hidden=null, visibility=visible, opacity=0.92, translateX(-311px) desktop / -101px mobile; app/globals.css:2491-2500 only transforms/dims it and app/ITrackApp.tsx:4134-4137 adds no inert/aria-hidden. Two H1s are exposed (list H1 + detail H1). Desktop tab order: skip link, 4 nav buttons, Log activity, then three under-screen stops (Add credential x=918, credential card x=-29 w=1112, Add another credential) before the detail's back button at stop 10; mobile: stops 3-5 are the hidden ones. The desktop screenshot shows the under screen is completely covered, so those stops are genuinely invisible. Bonus observation: after pushing the detail by keyboard, focus stays on the under-screen card (activeUnder=true).

findings.title: Closing any sheet that has an autoFocus field drops focus to <body>; Modal never sees React's autofocus
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:10606-10613 (previouslyFocused captured inside useEffect) and :10646-10648 (`dialog.querySelector('[autofocus]')`); autoFocus fields at :4919, :4970 (Set up a credential), :5444 (Log your submission), :5634 (acceptance), :8815, :8973 (Edit learning record / archive confirm), :9045, :9125 (Add/Edit personal task)
findings.evidence: focus-return.log: 18/18 cases fail — "Add credential", "Add another credential", "Add task", "Log renewal submission", "Log submission" × close via Escape / Close dialog / Cancel × desktop+mobile all end with activeElement=BODY while the trigger is still in the DOM; the 6 triggers whose sheets have no autoFocus (Log activity, Settings, Configure renewal check-ins, Edit requirement tags, Log an activity, Log qualifying learning) return focus correctly in every case. keyboard.log: Set up a credential and Add task open with focus on `section.modal-card`, not on the autoFocus input. Root cause: React implements `autoFocus` by calling .focus() during commit (before useEffect) and does not emit the `autofocus` attribute, so Modal records the already-focused input as "previouslyFocused" (disconnected on close → no restore) and its `[autofocus]` query never matches (so it overrides the intended field focus with the container).
findings.impact: After saving or cancelling the most common create flows (first credential, tasks, submissions) keyboard and screen-reader users are thrown to the top of the document and must re-navigate; the intended first-field focus is also lost. This is the shared Modal shell, so it will follow the client into the per-screen decomposition.
findings.recommendation: Capture the opener before commit: e.g. `const openerRef = useRef<HTMLElement|null>(null); if (openerRef.current === null) openerRef.current = document.activeElement as HTMLElement` in render (or pass the opener element in the open-state), and only call `dialog.focus()` when `!dialog.contains(document.activeElement)` so React autoFocus is honoured. Add a Playwright regression: open each sheet via keyboard, close via Escape/X/Cancel, assert focus returns to the trigger.
findings.verifier_note: Reproduced 18/18 failing cases + 12/12 passing controls (v-a11y-b.mjs, verify-b.log): Add task, Log renewal submission, Add credential x Escape/Close/Cancel x desktop+mobile all end with activeElement=BODY while the trigger is still in the DOM; Log activity and Settings (no autoFocus) return focus every time. My probe also shows document.querySelector('[role=dialog] [autofocus]') is null in every sheet (React does not emit the attribute) and initial focus lands on section.modal-card rather than the intended field, matching Modal at app/ITrackApp.tsx:10613-10616 (previouslyFocused captured in useEffect, after React's commit-phase autoFocus) and :10657-10659 / :10709-10711. Root cause and P2 stand: these are the first-credential and task/submission flows.

findings.title: SPA navigation never updates the page title or announces/moves focus on route change
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:1295-1400 (commitTab/push/pop router — replaceState/pushState only), 6809-6828 (NavButton: <button aria-current>), app/layout.tsx generateMetadata (static title); no document.title assignment anywhere in the client (grep)
findings.evidence: probe1: /, /credentials, /history, /profile all report document.title "iTrack — A clear path to renewal". probe2: activating the History nav button changes the URL to /history but focus stays on the nav button, title is unchanged and no live region fires; navigation is buttons, so the screen-reader links list contains only "Skip to content" and "Prepare packet" (probe1 links).
findings.impact: Screen-reader users get no confirmation that a tab switch or credential push happened and cannot tell tabs apart in the tab bar/history (WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled, 4.1.3 Status Messages); browser history entries are indistinguishable for everyone.
findings.recommendation: In `applyRoute` set `document.title` to `${screen title} · iTrack` (the H1 strings already exist per screen) and move focus to the new screen's H1 (tabIndex=-1) or its back control on push; alternatively keep a persistent polite live region and announce the screen name. Consider rendering tabs as real links (`<a href="/history">` with client-side interception) so they appear in link lists. Do this in the router so every decomposed screen inherits it.
findings.verifier_note: Verified (verify-a.log): document.title is 'iTrack — A clear path to renewal' on /, after activating History (URL becomes /history, focus stays on the nav button, no [aria-live]/[role=status]/[role=alert] node changes), after pushing a credential (URL changes, focus remains on the under-screen card) and after popping (focus drops to BODY). grep confirms no document.title assignment in app/ITrackApp.tsx; app/layout.tsx:24-27 defines a title template that nothing uses; the router at :1303-1392 only calls replaceState/pushState/history.back. The only <a> on /credentials is the skip link. Keeping P2: every screen-reader navigation in the app is silent.

findings.title: Every public-page CTA and text link fails AA contrast (white on #007aff 4.02:1, blue on grey 3.60:1) — live on itrackceu.com
findings.location: deploy/railway/pages/{landing,login,signup,reset,verify}.html shared <style>: `.btn-primary { background: var(--accent) #007aff; color:#fff }` (15px/600), `.btn-quiet`/`a { color: var(--accent) }`, `.badge` (#b97706 on #fff0d0), login.html:73 inline resend button; prod https://itrackceu.com/ serves byte-identical HTML (prod-landing.diff empty)
findings.evidence: axe color-contrast [serious] on all 20 public runs: landing 9 nodes (Log in, Get started, badge, Create your free account, I already have one, Sign up free, Start free today, coming-soon badge, Get in touch), login 4, login?error=unverified 5, signup 3, reset 3, verify 1 — 37 nodes per viewport. Exact ratios (public-contrast.mjs/tokens2.mjs): #fff on #007aff 4.02:1 (needs 4.5, text is 15px/600 so not "large"); #007aff on --paper #f2f2f7 3.60:1; #007aff on white 4.02:1; badge #b97706 on #fff0d0 3.27:1; "resend the link" #007aff on #fde3e4 3.31:1. The app already fixed the same pair: `.sidebar-add` uses --accent-control #0b6dd6 → 5.03:1 (semantics.log). Screenshot shots/public-landing-desktop.png.
findings.impact: The sign-up funnel's primary buttons and every secondary link are below AA for the ~8% of users with reduced contrast sensitivity, on the only pages a stranger sees before converting. WCAG 1.4.3 failure on the acquisition path.
findings.recommendation: One token change in the shared style block: use --accent-deep #0a63c9 for `.btn-primary` fill (5.77:1 with white) and for link/quiet-button text (≥5:1 on paper and card), and --ink-amber #795815 for the badge (the app's documented 5.8:1 on amber-soft). Carry the rule into the editorial redesign: any accent used as text or as a fill under 15px text must clear 4.5:1.
findings.verifier_note: Reproduced with axe on file:// renders of all five pages in 9 URL states x 2 viewports (v-a11y-c.mjs, verify-c.log, public-*.png): color-contrast serious on landing (9 nodes), login (4), login?error=unverified (5, incl. the 3.3:1 resend button), signup (3), reset (3), verify (1); axe classifies the 15px/600 buttons as 'normal' text so the large-text exemption does not apply. Independently computed ratios: #fff on #007aff 4.02, #007aff on #f2f2f7 3.60, on #fff 4.02, badge 3.27, resend 3.31; proposed --accent-deep #0a63c9 gives 5.77 and the app's --accent-control #0b6dd6 gives 5.03. curl with a Safari UA + Accept: text/html confirmed https://itrackceu.com/ , /login, /signup, /reset, /verify are byte-identical to deploy/railway/pages/*.html (prod-*.html, prod-*.headers). P2 is fair for the acquisition path, though the shortfall is modest and the fix is one token.

findings.title: Text inputs have no perceivable boundary: 1.58:1 border in light, 1.29:1 in dark, 1.28:1 on the public pages
findings.location: app/globals.css:4042-4051 (`.field input, .field select` border: var(--line-strong) on --white), tokens :20 (#cdcdd4) and :383/:391 (dark #3d3d44 on #2c2c2e); deploy/railway/pages/*.html `input { border: 1px solid var(--line) #e3e3e8; background:#fff }` on a white card
findings.evidence: semantics.log (Log activity sheet): border=rgb(205,205,212) bg=rgb(255,255,255) sheetBg=rgb(255,255,255) outline=none. Computed ratios: #cdcdd4 vs #fff 1.58:1; dark #3d3d44 vs #2c2c2e 1.29:1 and field fill vs card 1.22:1; public #e3e3e8 vs #fff 1.28:1. The field is otherwise indistinguishable from the card (same fill), so the border is the sole boundary. Screenshot shots/field-focus-light.png (unfocused fields blend into the sheet).
findings.impact: Low-vision users cannot see where fields begin or end on any form (Log activity, credential setup, login/signup); WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast requires ≥3:1 for a control's boundary when nothing else identifies it.
findings.recommendation: Give the redesign's input spec a boundary that clears 3:1 against its surface (e.g. a #767680-class edge, or a --paper-filled field on a --card surface with a 3:1 edge) in both schemes; if the current UI ships publicly before then, bump --line-strong for `.field` controls and the public `input` border.
findings.verifier_note: Measured myself (verify-a.log, 06-field-focus-light.png / -dark.png): .field input border rgb(205,205,212) on rgb(255,255,255) inside a white sheet = 1.58:1 (field bg vs card 1.00:1); dark: border rgb(61,61,68) on rgb(44,44,46) = 1.29:1, field vs card 1.22:1. Public pages: input border #e3e3e8 on #fff = 1.28:1 (signup computed borderColor rgb(227,227,232), card white). On login/signup the fields have labels above but no placeholder, so the border is the only thing that locates the 44px hit area; WCAG 1.4.11 asks for 3:1. Screenshot confirms unfocused app fields nearly vanish against the sheet.

findings.title: Form-field focus indicators are near-invisible compared with the app-wide 3px ring
findings.location: app/globals.css:4050 (`.field input { outline: none }`), :4058-4062 (focus = border-color --edge-focus + 3px rgba(78,149,224,0.13) glow), :4560-4562 (`.capture-button:focus-within` 3px rgba(19,122,233,0.36)), :1530-1534 (`.dental-checkpoint-form input:focus` outline 2px rgba(78,149,224,0.18))
findings.evidence: semantics.log focused field: border=rgb(93,149,208) outline=none boxShadow=rgba(78,149,224,0.13) 0 0 0 3px; capture label focus-within outline solid 3px rgba(19,122,233,0.36). Effective ratios over white (tokens2.mjs): glow 1.14:1, capture ring 1.62:1, dental outline 1.20:1; the border change #cdcdd4→#5d95d0 is a 1.99:1 difference on a 1px line. Everywhere else `:focus-visible` is a 3px #137ae9 ring (3.77–4.21:1). Screenshots shots/field-focus-light.png, shots/capture-focus-light.png.
findings.impact: Keyboard users lose track of focus precisely inside the forms, where most tabbing happens; the two hidden file inputs ("Take photo", "Choose photo or PDF") are tab stops whose only cue is the 36%-alpha ring. Passes 2.4.7 only nominally; fails WCAG 2.2 focus-appearance guidance (≥2px, 3:1).
findings.recommendation: Apply the shared `:focus-visible` ring (3px solid var(--focus-ring), offset 2px) to `.field input/select/textarea`, `.capture-button:focus-within` and dental inputs; keep the glow as decoration. Make this the one focus style in the redesign's token set.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: app/globals.css:4050 sets outline:none on .field input/select; focused field = border #5d95d0 (3.15:1 vs field bg light, 3.85:1 dark; only 1.99:1 / 2.98:1 change from the unfocused border) plus a 3px glow at 1.14:1 (light) / 1.48:1 (dark) effective contrast; .capture-button:focus-within ring 1.62:1 / 2.05:1; global :focus-visible at :716 is a 3px solid var(--focus-ring). Because the border colour change is itself visible (>3:1 against the field), WCAG 2.4.7 AA technically passes and only the 2.2 focus-appearance guidance is missed, so P3 is the right level.

findings.title: Window-level Escape closes every overlay at once and silently discards typed input in sheets without draft persistence
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:2371-2386 (window keydown Escape → closeActivityEntry + setCredentialOpen(false) + setSubmissionOpen(false) + … setTaskEditor(null))
findings.evidence: probe6: in "Add a personal task" typing "a11y-probe task" then Escape and reopening yields title "" (lost); keyboard.log: the same sequence in Log activity and Set up a credential preserves the value (draft persistence). keyboard.log: Escape while a <select> inside the sheet is focused closes the whole sheet (dialogs=0). The handler ignores event.defaultPrevented/IME composition and is not scoped to the open dialog.
findings.impact: A reflexive Escape (common when dismissing an autocomplete, a native picker, or an IME) wipes the task, submission, acceptance and edit-record forms with no confirmation, while identical-looking sheets keep their drafts — inconsistent and lossy for keyboard users.
findings.recommendation: Move Escape handling into Modal (listen on the dialog, `stopPropagation`, ignore when `event.defaultPrevented` or `event.isComposing`), and either persist drafts for every sheet or ask to discard when the form is dirty (a small confirm inside the sheet).
findings.verifier_note: Reproduced (verify-b.log): typing in 'Add a personal task' then Escape and reopening yields an empty title on desktop and mobile, while the Log activity draft is preserved (finder's keyboard.log; the draft-persistence code at app/ITrackApp.tsx:2358-2364 only covers the activity sheet). The window-level handler at :2371-2386 closes every sheet and ignores defaultPrevented/isComposing. One nuance: 'Escape while a <select> is focused closes the sheet' is only true when the select's popup is already closed, which is normal dialog behaviour (native <dialog> does the same), so that sub-point is not a defect; the data-loss inconsistency is.

findings.title: Snooze/Dismiss drop focus to <body>; confirmation toast is a transient, conditionally-mounted status region 25 tab stops away
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:7220-7236 (Snooze 7 days / Dismiss buttons remove their own row), :6485-6505 (toast rendered only while `toast` is set, role=status aria-live=polite, Undo button for archive/toggle actions), :2365-2369 (6000 ms auto-dismiss, no pause on hover/focus)
findings.evidence: probe6: pressing Enter on "Snooze 7 days" → toast "Reminder snoozed for one week." at 1105,810 (last of 25 tab stops), activeElement=BODY, reminders 2→1, toast gone after 6.5 s; no Undo for snooze/dismiss and no UI or API path to reverse (route.ts:12133 accepts only dismissed|snoozed). Live regions are mounted together with their content (toast, .row-saving, .draft-safety-note), which several screen readers do not announce reliably. Screenshot shots/toast-undo.png.
findings.impact: Keyboard/screen-reader users lose their place after every reminder action, may never hear the confirmation, and — for archive actions that do carry Undo — cannot reach Undo within the 6 s window (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable, 4.1.3).
findings.recommendation: After removing a row move focus to the next row or the "Needs attention" heading; keep one persistent (initially empty) polite live region in the shell and swap its text; pause the timer while the toast is hovered/focused and lengthen it (or make it sticky) whenever an Undo action is present. Product-side: consider an un-snooze/undo for reminders.
findings.verifier_note: Re-verified WITHOUT mutating data by intercepting POST /api/workspace (fulfilled {ok:true}) and filtering the snoozed key out of the following GET (v-a11y-b.mjs; sanity reload afterwards showed both demo reminders still present). Pressing Enter on 'Snooze 7 days': row removed (2→1), activeElement=BODY, toast role=status aria-live=polite mounted only while shown (0 persistent empty live regions), 16 Tab presses from body to reach it in my run, only a 'Dismiss notification' button (no Undo), and it was gone at 6.6 s despite being hovered (timer at :2365-2369 has no pause). route.ts:12133 accepts only dismissed|snoozed, so there is no un-snooze path. 'Cannot reach Undo within 6 s' is slightly overstated for sighted keyboard users but true for screen-reader users; P3 holds.

findings.title: Validation is native-bubble only: no aria-invalid, no persistent inline errors, requirements stated only after failure
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx Log activity form (required on title/totalUnits/allocatedUnits; only one aria-invalid at :4649 and one aria-describedby at :4650 in the whole client); deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:88-95 (password minlength=10 with no visible hint; "at least 10 characters" appears only in ?error=invalid flash)
findings.evidence: keyboard.log step 3: submitting the empty Log activity sheet → dialogs=1, focus moves to the title input, alerts=[], aria-invalid=[], native :invalid = FORM, title ("Please fill out this field."), totalUnits, allocatedUnits. Public pages: password rule absent before submit (signup.html), server-side error flashes are plain divs without role=alert/focus after the redirect.
findings.impact: Errors are announced once as a disappearing browser bubble and are not associated with the field afterwards; on signup the 10-character rule is discoverable only by failing (WCAG 3.3.1/3.3.2/3.3.3). Acceptable today, but it should not be the pattern the redesign inherits.
findings.recommendation: Define one error pattern for the redesign: inline persistent message per field tied with aria-describedby + aria-invalid, plus the existing ModalError alert as a summary that receives focus; on signup show "At least 10 characters" as a hint linked via aria-describedby and give the error flashes role="alert".
findings.verifier_note: Public half verified in verify-c.log: signup #password has minlength=10, no aria-describedby, and no visible '10 characters' text until ?error=invalid; all five .flash divs have role=none; login?error=unverified starts with focus on BODY, flash without role, email field empty. In-app half verified by code: exactly one aria-invalid (:4649) and one aria-describedby (:4650) in the whole client, everything else relies on native required bubbles (finder's keyboard.log step 3 shows alerts=[], aria-invalid=[]). P3 / carry-into-redesign is right.

` ×4 without aria-hidden; footer mailto link), signup.html `.note a`, shared `a { text-decoration: none }`

findings.title: Reminder urgency (overdue vs soon) is conveyed only by the aria-hidden dot colour

Confidence stays moderate because no overdue reminder could be rendered without mutating data.

findings.title: aria-label on generic <div>s is ignored by assistive tech (axe aria-prohibited-attr on every page)
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:6688 (`<div className="brand" aria-label="iTrack">`), :4885 (`<div className="mode-switch" aria-label="Credential setup mode">` wrapping two aria-pressed buttons), credential-packet-gaps div (`aria-label={`${trackedGapCount} tracked packet gaps`}`, ~:7600)
findings.evidence: axe incomplete aria-prohibited-attr: `.brand[aria-label]` on all 5 routes (both viewports/schemes), `.mode-switch` in the Set up a credential sheet, `.credential-packet-gaps` on the detail screen. aria-label is prohibited on role=generic, so "Credential setup mode" and "N tracked packet gaps" are never spoken.
findings.impact: The toggle pair loses its group name and the packet-gap count loses its summary label for screen-reader users; minor, but it is the only aria misuse in an otherwise clean tree.
findings.recommendation: Add role="group" to `.mode-switch` and `.credential-packet-gaps` (keeping the labels), and drop the aria-label from `.brand` (its visible text already names it).
findings.verifier_note: axe aria-prohibited-attr (needs-review) reproduced on / and the detail route in both viewports: aside > .brand[aria-label] / .mobile-header > .brand[aria-label] and .credential-packet-gaps (verify-a.log); code at app/ITrackApp.tsx:6688, :4885, :8079-8081. Two more instances of the same pattern that axe never saw because those states were not rendered: :10856 <div className="view-stack" aria-busy aria-label="Loading iTrack"> and :8901 <div className="read-only-status" aria-label="Current proof status">. aria-label is name-prohibited on role=generic per ARIA 1.2, so add role=group/status or drop the label.

findings.title: Type scale is px-only, so browser font-size preferences do not scale the UI
findings.location: app/globals.css:52-62 (--text-2xs…--text-lg 12–17px; body 15px), :5818 (10px tab-bar labels); deploy/railway/pages/*.html (13–16px, px throughout)
findings.evidence: All font-size tokens and the public stylesheets are declared in px; grep found no rem/em type sizes. Page zoom works (720px test clean), but a user who sets a larger default font in the browser gets no change.
findings.impact: Users who rely on the browser's default-font-size setting (rather than zoom) see no benefit; WCAG 1.4.4 is technically met via zoom, but the redesign is the moment to fix the unit.
findings.recommendation: Express the redesign's type scale in rem (root 100%) and keep the documented 10px tab-bar exception as 0.625rem with the 20px icon carrying the label.
findings.verifier_note: grep confirms 0 font-size declarations in rem/em and 48 in px in app/globals.css (the only relative one is a max(var(--text-control),1em) guard at :653); type tokens at :52-57 are 12-17px, body 15px, tab bar 10px at :5818; all public pages use px. No root font-size is declared, so a browser default-font-size preference has no effect while zoom works. Not a WCAG failure (1.4.4 is met via zoom), so P3 carry-into-redesign is correct.

findings.title: Windows High Contrast (forced-colors): checked/unchecked state is invisible and unchecked boxes show a check mark
findings.location: app/globals.css:1992-2005 (.custom-check color: transparent; .task-row.completed .custom-check = background only), :4141-4161 (.requirement-choice input opacity 0 + .requirement-check state = background tint), :4826-4847 (.segmented-field), :4907-4928 (.check-grid), :4418-4443 (.condition-options); the existing @media (forced-colors: active) block at :6606-6618 only covers .progress-track, .readiness-ring, .brand-mark and .mobile-add
findings.evidence: Playwright context with forcedColors:'active' (v-a11y-d.mjs / v-a11y-d2.mjs, verify-d.log, verify-d2.log). Home 'Packet readiness' checklist: all three .custom-check boxes render a black check glyph although only 1/3 tasks is completed (D-forced-home.png); computed on the unchecked rows: color rgb(0,0,0), svg stroke rgb(0,0,0) (normally rgba(0,0,0,0)), background transparent vs the checked row's rgb(255,255,255) — indistinguishable on a white Canvas. Log activity sheet: all five .requirement-check boxes show a check mark while only 'General Social Work' is checked (D-forced-log-activity.png); the 'Proof requirement' segmented radios (Add later / Not required) differ only by background rgb(255,255,255) vs rgba(255,255,255,0) and identical black border/text. In the normal scheme the same controls differ by tint fill and a white glyph (D-normal-log-activity.png).
findings.impact: Users on Windows High Contrast / forced-colors see every checklist task and every requirement checkbox as checked and cannot tell which proof/segment option is selected, so they will mis-log activities and mis-read renewal progress. The hidden native inputs (opacity 0) mean the platform's own high-contrast checkbox is never shown either.
findings.recommendation: In the redesign's control spec, draw state with something that survives forced colours: keep the native input visible (accent-color) or, for custom boxes, hide the glyph with display/visibility when unchecked (not color: transparent) and add a forced-colors rule (e.g. .custom-check, .requirement-check, .segmented-field span { forced-color-adjust: none } with input:checked + * { background: Highlight; color: HighlightText; border-color: Highlight }). A six-line addition to the existing @media (forced-colors: active) block fixes it today.

findings.title: Back (pop) from a pushed credential screen drops keyboard focus to <body> instead of returning to the originating card
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:8015 (push-back button lives inside the pushed screen), :4277-4283 (screen-pushed becomes screen-exiting and unmounts on finishScreenExit), :1384-1392 (pop only calls history.back()/commitTab; no focus management)
findings.evidence: verify-a.log, both viewports: open /credentials, focus the credential card, Enter (detail pushed, URL /credentials/demo-nj-lcsw-2026-253d00f801f4), then activate the 'Credentials' back control → URL /credentials, document.activeElement = BODY. The only .focus() calls in the client (:2294, :3887-3978, :5960, :7018, Modal) are unrelated to push/pop.
