findings.title: Gateway UA gate (kept only for the WKWebView 401 challenge) 401s iOS in-app browsers, link previewers, AI crawlers and HEAD requests on itrackceu.com
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:190-215 (wantsHtml + isBrowser = ua.includes('Safari/') || ua.includes('Firefox/'), 401 Basic fall-through); pinned by tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs:56-62, 83-87, 93-111 ('WKWebView shell (no Safari/ token) receives the 401 Basic challenge'); introduced by commit 84a2b24 'preserve iOS 401 challenge'
findings.evidence: Prod probes (prod-bot-gate.txt, prod-ua-gate.txt): GET / with Accept: text/html returns 401 text/plain + WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="iTrack" for WKWebView-style UAs used by the Gmail, LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram iOS in-app browsers (…Mobile/15E148 without a Safari/ token), for facebookexternalhit, Twitterbot, LinkedInBot, Slackbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-InspectionTool, legacy Googlebot/2.1, UptimeRobot and curl; HEAD / is 401 even with a Safari UA (method must be GET); /credentials with a WKWebView UA is 401 instead of 303 /login. Modern Googlebot/bingbot/Lighthouse/Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Samsung/CriOS/FxiOS pass (200). The only client that ever needed the 401 path is the retired shell (iTrack-iOS/ios/App/App/AuthChallengeHandler.swift:113-150 answers NSURLAuthenticationMethodHTTPBasic).
findings.impact: A stranger who taps an itrackceu.com link inside the Gmail/LinkedIn/Facebook/Instagram app on an iPhone gets a raw HTTP Basic login box instead of the landing page; shared links get no social preview; GSC's live URL Inspection and AI/search crawlers without a Safari token see a 401; uptime monitors using HEAD or curl read the site as down.
findings.recommendation: Classification: REMOVE. Delete the UA branch: any unauthenticated GET/HEAD / serves landing.html (no UA or Accept test); unauthenticated GET of an app path (/credentials, /credentials/*, /history, /profile) is a 303 to /login; everything else unauthenticated is 401 application/json {code:'authentication_required'} with NO WWW-Authenticate header. Replace the iOS regression test with its inverse (WKWebView, curl, facebookexternalhit and Twitterbot UAs receive the landing page) and drop the 'desktop Firefox still redirects' special case. Blast radius: two test blocks, no data, no env vars.
findings.verifier_note: Reproduced on prod with curl (prod-ua-matrix.txt): GET / with Accept: text/html returns 200 landing for Safari/Chrome/bingbot/modern-Googlebot UAs and 401 text/plain + WWW-Authenticate: Basic for the WKWebView-form UA, the Facebook (FBAN), Instagram and LinkedIn ([LinkedInApp]) in-app browser UAs (all lack a Safari/ token), facebookexternalhit, Twitterbot, LinkedInBot, Slackbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, legacy Googlebot/2.1, Google-InspectionTool and curl; HEAD / with a Safari UA is 401; /credentials with the WKWebView UA is 401 instead of 303 /login. Code at gateway.mjs:190-215 and tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs:56-62, 93-111 are exactly as cited; commit 84a2b24 confirmed in git log. One correction: Gmail iOS opens links in SFSafariViewController (Safari-form UA), so naming Gmail is probably wrong; the larger omitted victim is the app's own installed Home-Screen web app, whose UA has the same no-Safari/ form (see ios-coupling-M-01). Severity stands for a public self-serve launch.

findings.title: The PWA's own files sit behind the shell-oriented 401 and the manifest is fetched without cookies, so prod is not installable and never fires beforeinstallprompt
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:126-215 (no public-asset allowlist: only /healthz, /verify, /signup|/login|/reset, /auth/*, and the widget path bypass identity); app/layout.tsx:30 (manifest: '/manifest.webmanifest' renders <link rel="manifest"> with no crossorigin attribute — verified: local-app-checks.json manifestCrossorigin=null); public/sw.js:6-12 precache list; deploy/railway/serve.mjs:167 (the supervisor itself polls /manifest.webmanifest on the worker port, so the worker serves it; the proxy is what blocks it)
findings.evidence: Prod: /manifest.webmanifest, /sw.js, /offline.html, /icon-192.png, /apple-touch-icon.png, /og.png and /robots.txt all return 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Basic (prod-ua-gate.txt, prod-bot-gate.txt). Chrome experiment (manifest-credentials-probe2.json): with a session cookie set on the page, the <link rel=manifest> request arrives with sec-fetch-dest: manifest and cookie: null; the identical link with crossorigin="use-credentials" arrives with the cookie; /sw.js is fetched with the cookie (manifest-credentials-probe.json). So on prod even a signed-in Chromium user cannot load the manifest: no beforeinstallprompt, Profile's 'Install on this device' button (ITrackApp.tsx:9551-9570) never appears, Lighthouse installability fails. Safari's manifest credential behaviour was not tested.
findings.impact: The 'installable phone companion' promise (README.md:31, Profile copy) is broken on Chromium in production, and on iPhone Safari web push — the only reminder channel left once APNs goes — is only granted to Home-Screen installs, so anything that degrades install degrades reminders; /og.png 401 also means no social image can ever resolve.
findings.recommendation: Classification: KEEP-FOR-WEB (the assets) + fix the gateway. Proxy a fixed public allowlist without identity: /manifest.webmanifest, /sw.js, /offline.html, /icon-192.png, /icon-512.png, /apple-touch-icon.png, /og.png, /favicon.ico, /robots.txt (and a sitemap when one exists); add a gateway test that these are 200 unauthenticated while /api/* stays 401. Optionally also emit crossorigin="use-credentials" on the manifest link as belt-and-braces (Next's metadata API cannot, so it would be a manual <link> in layout.tsx).
findings.verifier_note: Prod: /manifest.webmanifest, /sw.js, /offline.html, /icon-192.png, /icon-512.png, /apple-touch-icon.png, /og.png, /favicon.ico, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml all answer 401 Basic without a session (prod-ua-matrix.txt); the real gateway.mjs run locally against a stub upstream does the same (gateway-bruteforce-verify.json, assets block). I reproduced the credentials claim independently with Chrome's own manifest fetcher (CDP Page.getAppManifest, manifest-cookie-verify2.json): a plain <link rel=manifest> is fetched with sec-fetch-dest: manifest and no Cookie header, the same link with crossorigin="use-credentials" carries the cookie, and /sw.js is fetched with the cookie. layout.tsx:30 goes through the metadata API so the rendered link has no crossorigin attribute (local: manifestCrossorigin=null). Two precision notes: the Profile button does render, labelled "How to install" when no beforeinstallprompt arrived (ITrackApp.tsx:9562) — it is only the "Install on this device" label that never appears; and robots.txt/sitemap do not exist in the repo at all (no public/robots.txt, no app/robots.ts), so the allowlist alone will not make those two resolve.

findings.title: HTTP Basic acceptance (ITRACK_USERS env users + DB accounts) and the Basic challenge on API 401s exist only for the shell; on the web they add a brute-force surface and a native browser login popup when a session expires
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:9-15 (basic cache constants), 30-41 (decodeBasic), 56-93 (basicCache, basicFailLimiter, basicIdentity), 180-184 (Basic fallback after session lookup), 211-215 (401 + WWW-Authenticate Basic); deploy/railway/serve.mjs:17-29 (docs), 49-68 (parseUsers), 86-99 (ITRACK_USERS ?? VIGILO_USERS ?? LANTERN_USERS, fail-closed exit 'not quietly 401 the iOS app'); tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs:31-33, 121-142, 170-173, 210-297; README.md:74-83; Dockerfile:1-4; Railway production var ITRACK_USERS (set; one entry keyed to Chris's personal Gmail address)
findings.evidence: Prod: GET /api/workspace with Accept: application/json and no or a garbage itrack_session cookie returns 401 text/plain + WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="iTrack", charset="UTF-8" (prod-session-expiry-probe.txt) — exactly what the SPA's fetch('/api/workspace') receives once the 30-day sliding session (auth.mjs SESSION_TTL_MS) lapses; browsers handle a same-origin fetch 401 Basic challenge with their own username/password dialog before ITrackApp.tsx:10906-10940 ('Your sign-in needs to be refreshed… Reload and sign in') renders. store.authenticate (auth.mjs:166-182, verified accounts) is reachable through Basic on every URL behind its own limiter (20 fails/15 min/IP, gateway.mjs:61) separate from /auth/login's 10/15 min. The signup spec states the purpose: 'checked against ITRACK_USERS env entries first, then against verified DB accounts (so the iOS wrapper can use either)'. VIGILO_USERS/LANTERN_USERS are code-only fallbacks (not set on Railway).
findings.impact: Web users whose session lapsed get a confusing raw browser auth dialog whose only valid input is email:password of a verified account; password guessing gets a second, page-less endpoint on every path; and because serve.mjs exits without ITRACK_USERS, deleting the variable before the code change crash-loops production.
findings.recommendation: Classification: KEEP-UNTIL-DATA-MIGRATED, then REMOVE. Order: (1) sign up on the web with the exact email in ITRACK_USERS — db/identity.ts:48-55 keys every user as sha256('license-lantern:'+email), so the same usr_ row and all D1/R2 data are reused — verify it and confirm the workspace loads via the session cookie (blocked until email works, see ios-coupling-13); (2) ship the gateway change: delete decodeBasic/basicIdentity/basicCache/basicFailLimiter, the users map, parseUsers and the fail-closed startup; respond 401 JSON with no WWW-Authenticate for non-HTML and 303 /login for HTML; make the client navigate to /login on a 401 workspace load instead of only offering reload; (3) only then delete ITRACK_USERS on Railway. findings.title: JS edge-swipe back (useEdgeSwipeBack + --screen-drag) exists for a WKWebView without native swipe-back; on the web the browser already owns that gesture
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:1415-1417 (EDGE_SWIPE_ZONE/COMMIT/ABANDON), 1430-1508 (document-level touchstart/move/end/cancel listeners), 2432 (useEdgeSwipeBack(screenStackRef, Boolean(detailCredential), nav.pop)), 2434-2443 (finishScreenExit clears --screen-drag); app/globals.css SCREEN STACK (--screen-drag, .screen-dragging, @keyframes screen-out 2550-2560); docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:154-157; pinned by tests/rendered-html.test.mjs:883-902
findings.evidence: The 2026-08-11 spec lists 'Edge-swipe back gesture on pushed screens (touch-tracked, interactive)' as a native-feel requirement for the shell. iOS Safari and Android gesture navigation perform history.back() themselves on a screen-edge swipe; the hook also treats touchcancel as an end (1479-1495) and commits at dx > 80, so where the page still receives the touch both fire (double pop). Not reproduced on hardware — Playwright cannot emulate system gestures — so flagged as a risk, not an observed defect. The nav stack underneath is correct web behaviour: local-app-checks2.json shows history.state {itrackNav:{depth:1,tab:'home'}} after a Home-card push with back label 'Home', browser back popping to /credentials, and cold /credentials/:id deep links resolving.
findings.impact: Document-wide touch listeners on every mobile touch, a possible double-back on real phones, and a moving target for the screen decomposition.
findings.recommendation: Classification: REMOVE the gesture hook, the drag custom property and its test pins; KEEP useNavigation (ITrackApp.tsx:1272-1410), app/lib/navigation.ts, the four route pages and tests/navigation.test.mjs. Whether the slide/parallax transition survives is a redesign decision.
findings.verifier_note: Code and pins exist as cited (ITrackApp.tsx:1415-1508, 2432-2443; rendered-html 883-902), but the premise that 'on the web the browser already owns that gesture' is false in the mode this product depends on: app/manifest.ts declares display: "standalone", the Profile screen tells iPhone users to Add to Home Screen to get alerts, and web.dev's PWA course plus firt.dev/brainhub document that iOS Home-Screen web apps have no browser back control and no swipe-navigation gesture — so this hook is the only back gesture the installed PWA has. The double-pop theory also cannot fire as described: onEnd commits only when the page still sees dx > 80px; when Safari or Android claims an edge gesture it cancels the touch within a few pixels, so touchcancel reaches rest(), not onBack(). The Ionic issues that surface in searches (#22299/#29733) are about in-browser swipe plus a framework gesture, not standalone mode. The nav stack underneath is verified (history.state {itrackNav:{depth:1,tab:'home'}} after a Home push with back label 'Home', browser back pops, cold deep link resolves). Classification should be carry_into_redesign (keep a JS back gesture for standalone), not REMOVE.

findings.title: Unauthenticated `/` swallows the query string and /auth/login always lands on `/`, so web-push notification deep links (`/?delivery=…`) are lost once a session lapses
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:202-209 (landing for pathname === '/' regardless of search; 303 /login with no return-to for other paths); deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:231 (redirect(res, "/") after login); public/sw.js:187-237 (notificationclick opens /?delivery=…); app/lib/webPush.ts:25-28 (ALLOWED_LAUNCH_PARAMETERS view/delivery)
findings.evidence: Prod GET /?delivery=abc with a Safari UA and no cookie returns 200 landing.html; auth-routes.mjs:231 redirects to '/' with no next parameter; sw.js opens the delivery URL on notification click and the client reads delivery/view from the launch URL. Sessions are 30-day sliding (auth.mjs:14) and push deliveries never refresh them, so the reminder that arrives after a month away lands on marketing copy and, after sign-in, on Home rather than the delivery it announced.
findings.impact: The channel replacing APNs loses its deep link on exactly the users push exists for — the ones not opening the app.
findings.recommendation: In the gateway PR that replaces the UA gate: carry the original URL through /login (a same-origin-validated ?next= app path) and honour it in /auth/login's redirect; serve landing only for a bare '/', or serve it with the query intact and let the sign-in link carry it.

findings.title: APNs private key, widget token and VAPID private key are handed to wrangler as `--var` command-line arguments, so they sit in the worker process's argv

findings.recommendation: When removing the APNS_*/ITRACK_WIDGET_TOKEN forwarding, switch the remaining VAPID values to a file-based mechanism on the /data volume (wrangler's .dev.vars-style file or --env-file) instead of argv.

findings.title: Outbound email is unconfigured: sign-up verification and password reset cannot be delivered (no Resend DNS records, no API key)
findings.location: DNS zone itrackceu.com (Name.com); deploy/railway/serve.mjs:235-238; deploy/railway/email.mjs:5; deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:158-166,222-223,245,262; deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:69
findings.evidence: dig: resend._domainkey.itrackceu.com TXT -> NXDOMAIN; send.itrackceu.com MX and TXT -> NXDOMAIN; _dmarc.itrackceu.com TXT -> NXDOMAIN; apex TXT/SPF -> 0 answers (dns.txt, confirmed at authoritative ns1kpv.name.com). email.mjs returns {error:'email-not-configured'} whenever RESEND_API_KEY or AUTH_EMAIL_FROM is unset; auth-routes.mjs:223 then redirects to /signup?sent=1&mail=down, whose copy is 'Your account was created, but the verification email could not be sent. Contact us and we'll activate you manually' (signup.html:69), and auth.mjs:176 refuses login for unverified accounts. My memory notes for this deploy (project_itrack_public_signup.md) record both variables still unset in Railway and the chosen sender as 'iTrack <no-reply@itrackceu.com>'.
findings.impact: Every public sign-up dead-ends at 'contact us' and password reset is equally dead; the only way anyone gets in today is Chris copying one-time links out of Railway logs. Nothing about the redesign changes this.
findings.recommendation: Chris, at Name.com DNS (copy exact values from Resend > Domains after adding itrackceu.com; region host as Resend shows it, typically us-east-1): (1) TXT resend._domainkey = p=<DKIM key from Resend>; (2) MX send = feedback-smtp.<region>.amazonses.com, priority 10; (3) TXT send = v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all; (4) TXT _dmarc = v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:support@itrackceu.com (move to p=quarantine after a few weeks of clean reports); (5) optional apex TXT v=spf1 -all once it is decided nothing sends with an apex envelope (add include:_spf.google.com instead if Chris will reply as support@ from Gmail). Then set Railway vars RESEND_API_KEY, AUTH_EMAIL_FROM="iTrack <no-reply@itrackceu.com>" and PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://itrackceu.com (see infra-05). Verify with real sign-ups to a Gmail and an Outlook address and confirm Authentication-Results shows dkim=pass (d=itrackceu.com), spf=pass (send.itrackceu.com) and dmarc=pass.
findings.verifier_note: Reproduced at the authoritative server (ns1kpv.name.com): resend._domainkey, send and _dmarc are NXDOMAIN, apex TXT/MX return 0 answers (infra-verify/dns.txt). Read the live service variables through Railway's API: the service defines exactly 10 variables (APNS_BUNDLE_ID/ENVIRONMENT/KEY_ID/PRIVATE_KEY/TEAM_ID, ITRACK_USERS, ITRACK_WIDGET_TOKEN, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY/PUBLIC_KEY/SUBJECT); RESEND_API_KEY and AUTH_EMAIL_FROM are absent, so email.mjs:5 returns email-not-configured, auth-routes.mjs:223 redirects to ?sent=1&mail=down, and auth.mjs:176 refuses login for unverified accounts. Two corrections/additions: (a) PUBLIC_BASE_URL is NOT needed - RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN already equals itrackceu.com in the running deployment (see infra-05); (b) it is worse than 'dead-ends at contact us': store.cleanup() (auth.mjs:15,239-243, called from every 15-minute fireCron) deletes unverified accounts after 7 days, and a retry inside that week hits ?error=email-taken, so every stranger's sign-up is silently discarded. Last 60 deploy-log lines contain no [auth] link line, i.e. nobody has signed up recently.

findings.title: support@itrackceu.com cannot receive mail (no MX): the only contact channel on the site bounces
findings.location: DNS zone itrackceu.com (Name.com); deploy/railway/pages/landing.html:141; deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:69
findings.evidence: dig MX itrackceu.com -> NOERROR with 0 answers at the resolver and at ns1kpv.name.com (dns.txt, dns-auth-and-local.txt). landing.html:141 links mailto:support@itrackceu.com; signup.html:69 tells users whose verification mail failed to 'Contact us'. With no MX, senders fall back to the A record (69.46.46.121:25, a Railway HTTP edge with no SMTP), so mail queues for days and then bounces.
findings.impact: Every support request, including the fallback path the product itself points users to when mail is down, silently fails; DMARC aggregate reports (infra-01) would be undeliverable too; a dead support address is a trust signal a stranger will notice.
findings.recommendation: Chris: add receiving. Cheapest on the current Name.com nameservers is Name.com's free Email Forwarding (it creates the apex MX records itself; requires Name.com NS, which is already the case) forwarding support@, postmaster@ and abuse@ to a real mailbox. Alternatives: ImprovMX (MX mx1.improvmx.com 10, mx2.improvmx.com 20) or move DNS to Cloudflare and use Email Routing. Resend's records live on send./resend._domainkey so they do not conflict with apex MX. Then send a test message and reply to it; add a Reply-To: support@itrackceu.com header to the transactional emails in auth-routes.mjs.
findings.verifier_note: dig MX itrackceu.com at the resolver and at ns1kpv.name.com: NOERROR, 0 answers; no apex TXT either (dns.txt). landing.html:141 links mailto:support@itrackceu.com and signup.html:69 tells mail-down users to 'Contact us' - and that flash contains no link or address at all, so the fallback is doubly dead. The RFC 5321 A-record fallback (69.46.46.121:25) was not probed, but the impact holds regardless: nothing at that address speaks SMTP.

findings.title: All user data (D1 SQLite, R2 blobs, auth.db, cookie secret) lives on one Railway volume with no evidence of any backup or restore procedure
findings.location: Dockerfile:17; deploy/railway/serve.mjs:46,204-225; volume layout in workerd-experiment.txt
findings.evidence: Observed state layout: /data/wrangler-state/v3/d1/miniflare-D1DatabaseObject/<sha>.sqlite (+ -wal/-shm, WAL mode) = every table; /data/wrangler-state/v3/r2/miniflare-R2BucketObject/metadata.sqlite + blob files = every uploaded certificate/PDF; /data/auth.db = accounts, scrypt hashes, sessions; /data/auth-session-secret = cookie signing key (AUTH_SESSION_SECRET was never set per memory). grep for backup|snapshot|restore across repo, docs, plans and memory: no script, no schedule, no runbook; the only backup ever taken (vigilo migration, 2026-07-27) was a tgz into an ephemeral scratchpad. Railway docs: volume backups exist only if enabled per service (manual, or Daily/Weekly/Monthly kept 6/27/89 days), restore only into the same project+environment, 'wiping a volume deletes all backups', manual backups limited to 50% of volume size; railway volume files download exists for off-platform copies. Three state paths derive from the single PERSIST_DIR value (serve.mjs:46,205,210,225).
findings.impact: A bad deploy, a PERSIST_DIR typo, an accidental volume wipe or a Railway incident loses every user's records and evidence with no recovery path, for a product whose pitch is 'never miss a renewal'.
findings.recommendation: Chris, today: take a manual backup, then enable Daily + Weekly volume backup schedules in the itrack service's Backups tab; check volume usage/size (evidence uploads are up to 10 MiB each; a 100%-full volume triggers an offline resize plus SQLITE_FULL errors). Chris: set AUTH_SESSION_SECRET as a sealed Railway variable so the signing key does not exist only on the volume. Code: add an off-platform nightly export (GitHub Actions cron running railway volume files download, or an in-container job using SQLite's VACUUM INTO / backup API for the three WAL-mode databases plus a tar of the R2 blob dir, encrypted, pushed to R2/B2/S3) and write + rehearse a restore runbook once in a scratch environment (verify login and an evidence download). Note the identity model helps: user ids are SHA-256(email), so a user whose auth.db row is lost recovers their D1 data by re-registering the same email, as long as the salt in db/identity.ts:49 never changes.
findings.verifier_note: Hard evidence via Railway GraphQL (infra-verify/railway-backups.txt, railway-graphql.txt): volume nurturing-analysis-volume, instance c10aff85 mounted at /data, sizeMB 50000, currentSizeMB 1131.78; volumeInstanceBackupList = [] and volumeInstanceBackupScheduleList = [] - zero backups, zero schedules. AUTH_SESSION_SECRET is not among the service's 10 variables, so the cookie-signing key exists only in /data/auth-session-secret. Railway docs (volumes/backups) confirm the Daily 6d / Weekly 27d / Monthly 89d retention, 50%-of-volume manual limit, same-project restore only, and 'wiping a volume deletes all backups'. The volume is 2.3% full, so the SQLITE_FULL scenario is remote; the no-backup scenario is real. The exact on-volume layout could not be listed (local Railway CLI 4.31.0 predates 'railway volume files'), but PERSIST_DIR/auth.db/secret paths in serve.mjs:46,205,210,225 are as stated.

findings.title: Landing page is gated on User-Agent/Accept: link-preview bots, AI crawlers, uptime monitors, HEAD requests and every iOS in-app browser get a 401 Basic prompt

findings.title: Public static assets are behind the auth wall: /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /favicon.ico, /og.png and icons redirect to /login (or 401)
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:175-210; public/ (no robots.txt, sitemap.xml or favicon.ico exist; the worker 404s them: workerd-experiment.txt)
findings.evidence: endpoints.txt: /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /favicon.ico, /og.png, /apple-touch-icon.png, /manifest.webmanifest, /sw.js, /offline.html -> 303 to /login for browsers and 401 for non-browser clients. landing.html carries only title/description/viewport meta: no <link rel=icon>, no canonical, no Open Graph tags; memory notes that public/og.png still reads 'Vigilo'.
findings.impact: Google treats a 401 robots.txt as absent (crawl allowed) but the sitemap is unreachable, the SERP favicon is missing, social cards have no image, and every crawler burns fetches on redirects into the login page.
findings.recommendation: Gateway: allow unauthenticated GET/HEAD for an explicit list (/robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /favicon.ico, /og.png, /icon-192.png, /icon-512.png, /apple-touch-icon.png, /manifest.webmanifest, /offline.html, /sw.js) by proxying them without identity headers or serving them from deploy/railway/pages. Add robots.txt (Disallow: /api/, Sitemap: https://itrackceu.com/sitemap.xml), a sitemap for /, /signup, /login, a real favicon.ico, and regenerate og.png. Canonical/OG metadata itself belongs to the landing-page redesign; the allowlist does not.
findings.verifier_note: Prod (prod-http.txt): /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /favicon.ico, /og.png, /apple-touch-icon.png, /manifest.webmanifest, /sw.js, /offline.html, /icon-192.png all 303 -> /login for a Safari UA and 401 for non-browser clients. Local worker (local-static.txt): robots.txt, sitemap.xml and favicon.ico 404 (do not exist in public/), while og.png, icons, sw.js, offline.html and manifest are served - so the allowlist alone would fix the latter group and three files still need creating. landing.html head carries only charset/viewport/title/description: no rel=icon, canonical or og:* tags (grep). One correction: public/og.png does NOT say 'Vigilo' - I viewed the PNG (dated 2026-08-03): iTrack mark, 'A clear path to renewal.' Drop the 'regenerate og.png' item; the memory note is stale.

findings.title: No HSTS and no security headers on any response (public pages or app); not HSTS-preload eligible
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:45-54 (servePage), 109-115 (proxy header pass-through); worker/vinext responses (workerd-experiment.txt)
findings.evidence: Response headers for https://itrackceu.com/ and /login: cache-control, content-type, date, server, x-railway-* only (http-basic.txt, endpoints.txt). Built worker responses with an identity header: Content-Type, Cache-Control, Vary only. Absent everywhere: strict-transport-security, x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, x-frame-options / CSP frame-ancestors, permissions-policy. hstspreload.org requirements: valid cert (yes), HTTP->HTTPS same-host redirect (yes, Railway 301 preserving path+query), HSTS header with max-age>=31536000 + includeSubDomains + preload (no), www served over HTTPS if a www record exists (none today, see infra-09).
findings.impact: First visits and bookmarks over http:// can be downgraded; an app that renders user-uploaded images/PDFs has no clickjacking or MIME-sniffing protection; the Secure cookie flag alone does not protect the first hop.
findings.recommendation: Add in gateway.mjs, applied to both static pages and proxied responses (one choke point): Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload; X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin; X-Frame-Options: DENY plus Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'; Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() (the OCR flow uses a file input, not getUserMedia). Give the redesigned static pages a real CSP (they currently rely on inline CSS/JS). Submit to hstspreload.org only after www resolves over HTTPS.
findings.verifier_note: Captured response headers for https://itrackceu.com/ (200), /login (200), /healthz, a 401 and a proxied worker response (/api/widget-summary 401 JSON): only cache-control, content-type, date, server: railway-hikari, vary, www-authenticate and x-railway-*; no Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/CSP, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy anywhere (prod-http.txt, misc-probes.txt). HTTP -> HTTPS is a 301 preserving path+query at the Railway edge (prod-http.txt). Cert: CN/SAN itrackceu.com only, Let's Encrypt YE1, ECDSA P-256, 2026-08-12 -> 2026-11-10, chain verify OK, TLS 1.2 and 1.3 negotiated (tls-edge.txt); I could not test TLS 1.0/1.1 refusal (local OpenSSL lacks them) - immaterial to the finding. Header injection point gateway.mjs:45-54 and :112 is as cited.

findings.title: www.itrackceu.com is NXDOMAIN; apex is a hand-coded A record to one Railway edge IP; no CAA; DNSSEC unsigned
findings.location: DNS zone itrackceu.com at Name.com (NS ns1kpv/ns2cvx/ns3gnv/ns4fpy.name.com); Railway custom-domain settings for service itrack
findings.evidence: www.itrackceu.com -> NXDOMAIN at the authoritative server (dns.txt, dns-auth-and-local.txt); curl to https://www.itrackceu.com fails at DNS. Apex: A 69.46.46.121 (TTL 60, Railway 'RLWY-HIKARI-01' per whois), no AAAA; _railway-verify.itrackceu.com TXT present (domain verified in Railway). itrackceu.com is served identically when pinned to 69.46.46.117 (the railway-domain IP) and 69.46.46.28 (edge-ip-interchange.txt), i.e. .121 is one of several interchangeable edge nodes, not a documented static IP; Railway's docs prescribe CNAME / ALIAS / CNAME-flattening for apex domains and Name.com supports ANAME records. Cert: CN=itrackceu.com, SAN itrackceu.com only, Let's Encrypt (YE1 -> ISRG Root X2/X1), ECDSA P-256, 2026-08-12 -> 2026-11-10, TLS 1.2/1.3 only (tls.txt). No CAA record; DNSSEC unsigned; whois: Name.com, created 2026-08-12, expires 2027-08-12, clientTransferProhibited.
findings.impact: All 'www.' traffic fails outright; if Railway retires or reassigns that edge IP the site goes dark until someone notices; any CA may issue for the domain; the Name.com account is a single point of failure for both registration and DNS.
findings.recommendation: Chris (Name.com + Railway): replace the apex A record with an ANAME pointing at the CNAME target shown in Railway's custom-domain panel; add www.itrackceu.com as a second custom domain in Railway (Hobby allows 2 per service) with the CNAME and _railway-verify TXT it provides; add CAA 0 issue "letsencrypt.org" (Railway issues Let's Encrypt certs) plus CAA 0 iodef mailto:support@itrackceu.com; enable DNSSEC once the above is stable; confirm auto-renew, registrar lock and 2FA on the Name.com account. Code: 301 www -> apex in the gateway (infra-05). Alternative that solves apex, inbound mail (Email Routing), CAA and DNSSEC in one move: move nameservers to Cloudflare (free).
findings.verifier_note: www.itrackceu.com NXDOMAIN at ns1kpv.name.com and curl fails to resolve; apex A 69.46.46.121 TTL 60, no AAAA, no CAA, no DNSKEY/DS, NS ns1kpv/ns2cvx/ns3gnv/ns4fpy.name.com, _railway-verify TXT present; whois: Name.com, created 2026-08-12, expires 2027-08-12, clientTransferProhibited, DNSSEC unsigned (dns.txt, tls-edge.txt). Edge interchangeability reproduced: pinning itrackceu.com to 69.46.46.121, .117 (the railway.app IP) and .28 all return 200 with an identical 7723-byte body. Railway docs (networking/domains/working-with-domains) confirm apex domains are expected to use CNAME flattening or dynamic ALIAS, and that Hobby allows 2 custom domains per service (Pro 20). The 50 GB volume suggests a paid plan, so adding www is not limit-bound.

findings.title: No health check, uptime monitoring or alerting; /healthz never touches the worker; a crash loop ends in silent downtime
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:130-134; deploy/railway/serve.mjs:152-175; repo root (no railway.json/railway.toml, so Railway settings are dashboard-only and unverifiable here)
findings.evidence: /healthz returns 'ok' from the proxy without probing 127.0.0.1:8787 (endpoints.txt shows 200 in ~110 ms). Railway docs: the healthcheck path is used only at deploy time, never for continuous monitoring; default restart policy is On Failure with a maximum of 10 restarts. serve.mjs exits the whole process when wrangler exits (152-155) or never becomes ready within 120 s (164-175), so after 10 crashes the service stays down with nothing watching. GET / with an UptimeRobot UA returns 401 (ua-matrix.txt), so a naive monitor on the homepage would page constantly or be silenced. The gateway writes no per-request log line; wrangler debug logs go to /tmp/wrangler-logs (ephemeral); there is no error tracker.
findings.impact: An outage (crash loop, full volume, revoked Resend key, stuck cron) is discovered by users or by chance, and there is no request-level log to diagnose it afterwards.
findings.recommendation: Chris (Railway settings): Healthcheck Path = /healthz; Restart Policy = Always; add an external monitor (UptimeRobot / Better Stack / Railway's Uptime Kuma template) doing GET https://itrackceu.com/healthz every 1-5 min with email+SMS alerts, plus TLS-expiry and DNS checks. Code: make /healthz probe the worker (GET 127.0.0.1:8787/manifest.webmanifest with a 2 s timeout, 503 on failure) and optionally the auth DB; emit one access-log line per request (method, path, status, ms, client ip) so Railway logs are usable; log the cron result on every run (infra-14).
findings.verifier_note: Verified via Railway GraphQL serviceInstance: healthcheckPath null, healthcheckTimeout null, restartPolicyType ON_FAILURE, restartPolicyMaxRetries 10, drainingSeconds null; no railway.json/toml in the repo. Railway docs (deployments/healthchecks) state the path is 'not used for continuous monitoring'. /healthz answers from the proxy without touching the worker (gateway.mjs:130-134; prod 200 in 120 ms); serve.mjs:152-155/164-175 exit the process on wrangler exit or 120 s readiness failure; UptimeRobot/Better Uptime UAs get 401 on / (ua-matrix.txt). Two corrections: Railway DOES keep per-request HTTP logs at the edge (my own probes appear as 'GET / 401 6ms', 'HEAD /login 401 2ms'), and wrangler logs every proxied request ('[wrangler:info] GET /api/widget-summary 401 Unauthorized (3ms)' in deploy logs, which are retained and were readable for today), so 'no request-level log' is overstated; what is missing is the gateway's own decision log and any alerting. No error tracker found (grep sentry/bugsnag/datadog/logtail/posthog: none).

findings.title: Every push to main auto-deploys to production with no CI gate, no branch protection and no staging environment
findings.location: README.md:73-83; repo root (no .github/ directory); Dockerfile:14
findings.evidence: ls .github -> No such file or directory; package.json defines typecheck, lint and test (232 tests per memory) but nothing runs them before Railway builds; the Docker build runs only npm run build. Railway's 'Wait for CI' needs a GitHub workflow with on: push: branches: [main], which does not exist. One environment (production) bound to the volume; the memory rule 'local Docker build/run before deploy' is manual.
findings.impact: A change that builds but breaks at runtime (a gateway routing bug, a migration error) ships straight to users, and with a volume attached each deploy is already a mini-outage (infra-13), so bad deploys cost twice during the redesign's high-commit cadence.
findings.recommendation: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml (Node 22: npm ci, npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm test, docker build) on push and pull_request; enable 'Wait for CI' on the Railway service; protect main (PRs only, required checks). Consider a staging Railway environment with its own volume for redesign screens.
findings.verifier_note: ls .github -> No such file or directory; no railway.json/railway.toml; package.json defines typecheck/lint/test (15 test files) but the Dockerfile runs only npm ci + npm run build, and the build log for deployment b8b32146 shows the 6-step Dockerfile build with no test stage (the dashboard 'Builder: RAILPACK' setting is overridden by the detected Dockerfile). list_deployments shows commits deploying as pushed (10 deployments 08-04 to 08-12), one environment (production) bound to the single volume. Railway docs (deployments/github-autodeploys) confirm 'Wait for CI' requires a workflow with on: push: branches: [main]. Borderline P2/P3 for a solo project, but every bad push is an immediate prod outage with a volume-bound deploy, so P2 stands.

findings.title: iOS-only env vars, routes, tables, secrets and Basic-auth plumbing to delete once the shell is retired (full env-var audit)
findings.location: deploy/railway/serve.mjs:17-29,49-99,108-124; deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:9-15,56-93,146-149,190-215; worker/index.ts:17-22,59-124,172,245; app/api/apns-token/route.ts; app/api/widget-summary/route.ts; app/lib/apnsDelivery.ts, apnsJwt.ts, apnsPush.ts, apnsRegistration.ts, widgetSummary.ts; db/runtime.ts:461-495; drizzle/0012_redundant_kate_bishop.sql; tests/apns-*.test.mjs (4 files), tests/widget-summary.test.mjs, tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs:57-148
