Deploy logs show the APNs channel still runs every 15 min with devices=1 (Chris's phone).

findings.title: Redeploys are not zero-downtime (volume) and shutdown is abrupt; sessions do survive; boot-time cron is deduplicated
findings.location: deploy/railway/serve.mjs:157-162,164-175,251-254; Railway service settings (RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS, healthcheck path)
findings.evidence: Railway docs: 'there will be a small amount of downtime when re-deploying a service that has a volume attached, even if there is a healthcheck endpoint configured'; SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL grace defaults to 0 s; without a healthcheck path a deployment is marked Active on container start, but serve.mjs only listens after waitForWorker resolves. The SIGTERM handler calls process.exit(0) immediately with no server.close(), so in-flight requests (evidence uploads up to 12 MB, D1 writes) are severed; SQLite atomicity prevents corruption but clients see network errors. Cold start of the built worker measured 1.05 s locally (workerd-experiment.txt). Sessions (auth.db) and the cookie secret file persist on the volume, so users stay logged in; in-memory rate-limit and Basic caches reset harmlessly; fireCron runs at boot (serve.mjs:253) but push_delivery_ledger uses INSERT OR IGNORE with a unique key (pushDelivery.ts:783-793), so no duplicate reminders.
findings.impact: A few seconds of 502s and any in-flight upload lost on every deploy; tolerable at launch, but the redesign will deploy often.
findings.recommendation: Code: graceful shutdown (stop accepting, server.close(), wait up to ~10 s for in-flight requests, then kill wrangler). Chris: RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS=15 and Healthcheck Path=/healthz; deploy in low-traffic windows. True zero-downtime requires moving state off the single volume (real D1/R2, or managed Postgres + object storage), which is a later architectural call.
findings.verifier_note: Code verified: serve.mjs:157-162 SIGTERM handler kills wrangler and calls process.exit(0) with no server.close(); :164-175 120 s readiness loop; :251-253 listen only after waitForWorker, then fireCron at boot; push_delivery_ledger dedupe via INSERT OR IGNORE (pushDelivery.ts:783) on the unique index push_delivery_ledger_occurrence_unique (db/runtime.ts:455). Railway docs (deployments/healthchecks) confirm 'a small amount of downtime when re-deploying a service that has a volume attached, even if there is a healthcheck endpoint configured'; deployment-teardown docs describe RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS; the service's drainingSeconds is unset (null). The specific '0 s default' figure was not found in the docs I read - immaterial. The Dockerfile CMD runs node directly, so SIGTERM does reach serve.mjs (Railway's nodejs-sigterm-handling page warns npm would swallow it).

findings.title: Reminder cron is a 15-minute in-process timer capped at 8 pushes / 64 subscriptions per run, and stops entirely if Railway Serverless (app sleeping) is on
findings.location: deploy/railway/serve.mjs:47,177-199,252-253; app/lib/pushDelivery.ts:57-61,721-745,896-903; worker/index.ts:105-115,136-191
findings.evidence: setInterval(fireCron, 15 min) is not wall-clock aligned and its phase resets on every restart. Each run scans at most SUBSCRIPTION_SCAN_BUDGET=64 subscriptions (ordered by updated_at, bumped after scanning, so it round-robins) and delivers at most MAX_DELIVERIES_PER_RUN=8 notifications via roundRobinDeliveries, deferring the rest: a hard ceiling of 32 pushes/hour, 768/day. Users pick a local push hour; with 100 users on 09:00 the last one is delivered ~3 h 10 min late, with 500 more than 15 h late. Railway docs: Serverless sleeps a container after ~5-10 min without outbound packets, and the cron's POST to 127.0.0.1 is loopback, not outbound, so if that setting is ever enabled reminders halt until a visitor wakes the container. A failed run only prints '[cron] scheduled delivery -> 500' or the 'appears stuck' warning; nothing alerts.
findings.impact: The product's core promise (timely reminders) degrades silently as soon as a few dozen users share a reminder hour, and one dashboard toggle can stop reminders completely.
findings.recommendation: Chris: confirm Serverless/App Sleeping is OFF for the itrack service. Code: on Railway there is no cron CPU limit, so run the timer every 1-5 min aligned to the wall clock and raise MAX_DELIVERIES_PER_RUN and SUBSCRIPTION_SCAN_BUDGET (or loop until the ready queue drains within a time budget); log deferred>0 and any non-200 as warnings, expose last-run status on /healthz (infra-10) so the external monitor catches a stuck cron.
findings.verifier_note: Constants verified: SUBSCRIPTION_SCAN_BUDGET=64, MAX_DELIVERIES_PER_RUN=8, READY_FETCH_LIMIT=32 (pushDelivery.ts:58-61), scan ORDER BY updated_at LIMIT 64 then bump (:721-750), roundRobinDeliveries(…, 8) and deferred accounting (:898-902); apnsDelivery.ts:59-60 mirrors 64/8. CRON_INTERVAL_MS 15 min setInterval (serve.mjs:47,252). Deploy logs show the cron firing at :11/:26/:41/:56 with 200 (not wall-clock aligned, as stated), scanned=0 - there are currently zero web-push subscriptions in production. Strengthening evidence: push_hour_local defaults to 9 (db/runtime.ts:392, db/schema.ts:505, ITrackApp.tsx:3626), so every user in a timezone shares one slot and the 8-per-run cap bites at the 9th user. One correction: sleepApplication=false in the service instance, so the 'stops entirely under Serverless' half is hypothetical (Railway docs confirm the loopback-not-outbound mechanism should it ever be enabled). P2 rests on the cap alone.

findings.title: Raw verification and password-reset links (one-time tokens) plus user emails are written to Railway logs whenever email fails, which today is always
findings.location: deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:158-166 (deliver), 222, 245, 262; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-11-itrack-public-signup.md:2141-2183 (Task 7 instructs reading links from logs)
findings.evidence: deliver() logs `[auth] ${kind} link for ${email}: ${message.link} (email ${result.error})` on any non-ok send; with Resend unconfigured every signup and every reset request prints the full 24 h verify / 1 h reset URL to stdout, i.e. into the Railway log stream; the plan formalises reading tokens from the deploy logs as the onboarding path. After Resend is live the same line fires on any transient send failure.
findings.impact: Anyone with Railway project access or a log export can take over accounts via logged reset links; user emails (PII) accumulate in logs.
findings.recommendation: Once infra-01 is done, log only `[auth] <kind> email send failed` with a hashed email and no link; if a manual-activation path is still wanted, add an admin-only resend action instead. Also consider consuming /verify on POST (a click-through page) since mail scanners pre-fetch GET links, a deferred item already noted in the plan.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: auth-routes.mjs:158-166 logs '[auth] <kind> link for <email>: <link> (email <error>)' on any failed send, reached from :222, :245 and :262, and the plan (lines 2168-2180) instructs reading the link from Railway logs; deploy logs are retained and readable via the API (I fetched today's), though the last 60 lines contain no such line. Downgraded because the exposure is narrow: the only Railway project member is the owner, verify tokens are single-use (auth.mjs:105-116) and expire in 24 h, reset tokens in 1 h, and once infra-01 lands the line fires only on transient failures. Still remove the link from the log and log a hashed address instead.

findings.title: Production runs `wrangler dev` on an unpinned base image with its runtime in devDependencies; demo identity is granted on Host header alone
findings.location: Dockerfile:6,10-16,21; deploy/railway/serve.mjs:108-150; package.json (wrangler 4.92.0 in devDependencies); db/identity.ts:18-26,77-84
findings.evidence: FROM node:22-bookworm-slim is a floating tag; devDependencies are installed only because NODE_ENV=production is set after npm ci (Dockerfile:11 vs 16), so adding NODE_ENV as a Railway build variable would silently drop wrangler and break startup; wrangler prints 'update available 4.130.0' (workerd-experiment.txt); D1 and R2 are miniflare's local SQLite emulations, never the cloud services; VAPID/APNs private keys are passed as `--var NAME:value` command-line arguments (visible in the container's process list). The worker grants a read/write demo identity ('Alex Morgan') to any request without identity headers whose URL host is localhost/127.0.0.1 (db/identity.ts:77-84): reproduced unauthenticated GET / and /api/workspace -> 200 against the built worker. Not reachable today: Railway's edge answers 404 for Host: localhost over HTTP/1.1 and h2 (www-and-verify.txt), the gateway forwards the real Host, and the only identity-less proxied path (/api/widget-summary) is token-gated. It becomes exploitable the moment a gateway refactor lets Node default the upstream Host header to 127.0.0.1:8787.
findings.impact: Non-reproducible builds, a development server as the production runtime (every wrangler bump is an untested runtime change), and a latent fail-open auth path waiting for a refactor.
findings.recommendation: Pin the image digest (node:22.22.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:...), move wrangler to dependencies or run workerd directly, load worker secrets from a `.dev.vars`-style file on the volume instead of argv, gate the demo identity on an explicit env flag (e.g. ITRACK_DEMO_IDENTITY=1, never set in prod) and have the gateway overwrite `host` with the canonical public host. Revisit whether the Workers build target still earns its keep when state lives on Railway anyway.
findings.verifier_note: Dockerfile:6 floating node:22-bookworm-slim, :11 npm ci before :16 ENV NODE_ENV=production; wrangler 4.92.0 in devDependencies; serve.mjs:108-124 passes VAPID/APNs/widget secrets as --var NAME:value argv; db/identity.ts:77-84 grants the Alex Morgan demo identity on localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 hosts - reproduced on the running dev worker (GET /api/workspace -> 200, 13.7 KB, no identity headers). Railway edge returns 404 for Host: localhost over HTTP/1.1 and h2, the gateway forwards the real Host (gateway.mjs:96,110), and the only identity-less proxied path is token-gated, so it stays latent. Build log for b8b32146 confirms the Dockerfile is what runs. One correction: a Railway-side NODE_ENV variable would not reach 'npm ci' in a Dockerfile build unless the Dockerfile declares ARG NODE_ENV, so that hazard is overstated. Added evidence for the 'dev server as prod runtime' point: service_metrics show the idle container at ~1.4 GB RSS (24 h average 1.39 GB) at 0.2% CPU.

findings.title: Launch-readiness checklist with owner per item (Chris vs. code)
findings.location: Railway service itrack (project 0d9241ed-5a83-4314-b790-06946473ea89), Name.com DNS for itrackceu.com, deploy/railway/*, Dockerfile, .github/
findings.evidence: Aggregates infra-01 through infra-16; every item traces to an observation in the assets listed for this dimension.
findings.impact: Without these, a stranger who lands on itrackceu.com today cannot finish sign-up, cannot email support, may hit a 401 dialog from an in-app browser, and the only copy of any data they do create is unbacked-up.
findings.recommendation: CHRIS (accounts, DNS, dashboard): (1) Resend: add itrackceu.com, publish resend._domainkey TXT, send MX+TXT, _dmarc TXT; create API key; set RESEND_API_KEY, AUTH_EMAIL_FROM='iTrack <no-reply@itrackceu.com>', PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://itrackceu.com [infra-01/05]. (2) Inbound: Name.com email forwarding (or ImprovMX/Cloudflare) for support@, postmaster@, abuse@; send+reply test [infra-02]. (3) Rotate/remove ITRACK_USERS now; decide repo visibility; later delete APNS_*, ITRACK_WIDGET_TOKEN and revoke the APNs key [infra-03/12]. (4) Manual volume backup today, then Daily+Weekly schedules; check volume usage; set AUTH_SESSION_SECRET as a sealed variable [infra-04]. (5) Railway settings: Healthcheck Path=/healthz, Restart Policy=Always, RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS=15, Serverless OFF, 'Wait for CI' once the workflow exists [infra-10/11/13/14]. (6) External uptime monitor on GET /healthz + TLS-expiry + DNS checks with alerts [infra-10]. (7) DNS: apex A -> ANAME to Railway target; add www custom domain (CNAME + _railway-verify TXT); CAA letsencrypt.org; DNSSEC; verify auto-renew, lock and 2FA at Name.com (or move NS to Cloudflare) [infra-09]. (8) After www and HSTS ship: optionally submit hstspreload.org [infra-08]. CODE: (9) Remove iOS shell support: APNs stack, widget route/exemption, Basic auth, ITRACK_OPEN_IDENTITY, UA/Accept gate, related tests; startup requires only the session store [infra-06/12]. (10) Unauthenticated allowlist for robots.txt, sitemap.xml, favicon.ico, og.png, icons, manifest; add robots/sitemap/favicon; regenerate og.png [infra-07]. (11) HSTS + X-Content-Type-Options + Referrer-Policy + X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors + Permissions-Policy in the gateway [infra-08]. (12) 301 www and railway.app hosts -> https://itrackceu.com [infra-05/09]. (13) Deep /healthz, per-request access log, graceful SIGTERM shutdown [infra-10/13]. (14) Cron every 1-5 min wall-clock aligned, raise per-run caps, warn on deferred/failed runs [infra-14]. (15) Stop logging verify/reset links [infra-15]. (16) .github/workflows/ci.yml (typecheck, lint, test, docker build) + branch protection [infra-11]. (17) Off-platform nightly backup job + rehearsed restore runbook [infra-04]. (18) Pin base image digest, wrangler into dependencies, secrets via file not argv, env-gate the demo identity, canonical upstream Host [infra-16]. (19) Update README Deployment section to the surviving variable list [infra-12].
findings.verifier_note: Not an independent finding - an aggregate of infra-01..16, so it cannot be verified beyond its parts. Corrections to carry into the checklist: item (1) PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unnecessary (RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN is already itrackceu.com); item (10) drop 'regenerate og.png' (already iTrack-branded); item (5) Serverless is already OFF and the healthcheck/restart/draining values are confirmed unset/ON_FAILURE-10/unset; item (12) there are two Railway-generated domains to redirect or delete, not one; add the sign-out bug (infra-M-01) to the code list ahead of everything except infra-03/01/04.

findings.title: Self-serve users cannot sign out: the only Sign out control links to /signout-with-chatgpt, a ChatGPT-hosting leftover that neither the gateway nor the worker serves
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:9257-9263; deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:158-161,175-188; deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:189-195; app/api/workspace/route.ts:12293 (and catalog/route.ts:31, export/route.ts:32, export/packet/route.ts:90, evidence/_shared.ts:98)
findings.evidence: The Profile screen renders Sign out for every non-demo user; grep finds no other logout/sign-out reference in the 11k-line client or in deploy/railway/pages. The gateway's logout exists only as POST /auth/logout (auth-routes.mjs:190-195 answers 404 to GET), and any request carrying a valid session cookie to another path is proxied to the worker (gateway.mjs:180-188). The worker has no such route: the production build's route list (build log 2026-08-12) is /, /api/*, /credentials, /credentials/:id, /history, /profile, and GET http://localhost:3000/signout-with-chatgpt on the running dev worker returns 404 'Not Found' (9 bytes; infra-verify/volume-and-client.txt). Railway's HTTP log already records a real hit, 'GET /signout-with-chatgpt 303' at 2026-09-10 13:28 UTC (anonymous, redirected to /login). The demo identity sees 'Local preview' instead of the button (ITrackApp.tsx:9255), which is why local testing never exercised it. Five API 401 bodies still say 'Sign in with ChatGPT…' (the SPA hides them behind its own copy, WorkspaceLoadFailure at :10906-10920). Not reproduced with a live production session because prod login is off-limits; the routing is deterministic.
findings.impact: A self-serve user who clicks Sign out lands on a bare 'Not Found' page and remains signed in for the 30-day sliding session (auth-routes.mjs:6; auth.mjs:205-207 extends it on every request); on a shared or borrowed computer the workspace and evidence files stay open with no way to end the session short of clearing cookies.
findings.recommendation: Replace the anchor with <form method="post" action="/auth/logout"><button type="submit">Sign out</button></form> (same-host Origin satisfies the gateway's CSRF check, the route deletes the session row and clears the cookie); delete the 'Sign in with ChatGPT' strings in the five API routes; add a gateway test that a session-bearing POST /auth/logout clears the cookie and a following GET / with a Safari UA serves the landing page. Do this before the profile screen is redesigned - the redesign should inherit a working control, not rediscover the bug.

findings.title: Sign-up reveals whether an email already has an account (?error=email-taken)
findings.location: deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs:219; deploy/railway/pages/signup.html:70
findings.evidence: POST /auth/signup with an existing address redirects to /signup?error=email-taken, whose flash reads 'That email already has an account. Log in instead.' The sign-up limiter is 5/hour/IP (auth-routes.mjs:141) keyed on the last x-forwarded-for entry (:70-81). The other routes are already uniform - request-reset always answers ?sent=1 (:242-246), resend always ?resent=1 (:258-264), and login reports 'unverified' only after the password matched (auth.mjs:173-176) - so sign-up is the sole enumeration oracle.
findings.impact: Anyone can test, at 5 addresses per hour per IP, whether a given licensed professional has an iTrack account; low impact for this product today, but it is a free fix once email works and cheaper to make now than after the redesign copies the flash.
findings.recommendation: Once Resend is live, treat a taken email exactly like a new sign-up (redirect to ?sent=1) and email the existing account a 'you already have an account - reset your password' message instead; keep the visible copy identical for both cases.

findings.title: "Today" is computed in UTC on the client and reminder time zone defaults to "UTC": every US user gets tomorrow's date as the default completion/submission/acceptance/snooze date after ~5-8 pm local, and push check-ins fire at 9:00 UTC (2-5 am US) until the user hand-types an IANA zone
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx:403 (todayIso = new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)); consumers :1668 (NREMT submission date), :1703/:1765 (activity draft completionDate), :3052 (OCR suggestion reset), :3542, :3644 (snoozedUntil = addDaysIso(todayIso(), 7)), :5453 (Log your submission default), :5637 (acceptance default); :434-435 + app/lib/readiness.ts:46 (countdown uses LOCAL end-of-day, so the same screen disagrees with itself); app/lib/reminders.ts:215-218 and app/api/workspace/route.ts:2408-2411, 12203-12206 (timeZone falls back to "UTC"); app/ITrackApp.tsx:5959 (deviceTimeZone() only wired to a button inside the Manage reminders modal); app/api/export/route.ts:112 (CSV filename date also UTC)
findings.evidence: Playwright with page.clock.setFixedTime('2026-09-10T02:30:00Z') and timezoneId America/New_York: page reports 'Wed Sep 09 2026 22:30:00 GMT-0400' yet the Log-activity sheet's completionDate input value is '2026-09-10' (critic/critic-probe.json; critic/clock-log-sheet.png shows '09/10/2026' under the helper 'Must fall within the selected renewal cycle'); the hero on the same page counts '83 DAYS TO RENEWAL' from local time. The server rejects dates after the deadline or outside the cycle: route.ts:3381-3386 ('The activity date must not be after the target renewal deadline') and :1623-1632 (activity_outside_cycle, 409). Fresh user GET /api/workspace returns reminderPreferences {timeZone:'UTC', pushHourLocal:9, leadDays:[90,30,7,1]} with no client auto-capture of the device zone.
findings.impact: For a deadline tracker this is a silent data-correctness bug in the core flow: a course logged on the evening of the deadline day defaults to a date the server refuses (or, mid-cycle, is recorded on the wrong day in the audit trail), snoozes are a day long or short, and the first push reminder a US user ever gets arrives in the middle of the night, which trains them to disable alerts.
findings.recommendation: Replace todayIso() with a local-date helper (year/month/day from the Date object, not toISOString) and use it everywhere the grep lists; on first workspace load, if reminderPreferences.timeZone is the UTC fallback, persist Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone automatically via updateReminderPreferences and show it on Profile; keep the countdown local. Add a unit test that runs the helpers at 23:30 in America/Los_Angeles.

findings.title: Dependency hygiene is unaudited: npm audit reports 25 known vulnerabilities (1 critical, 15 high) and several are in the packages that ARE the production runtime (wrangler/miniflare/undici/ws), with no Dependabot, Renovate, or CI audit to notice the next one
findings.location: package.json (wrangler 4.92.0, vite 8.0.13, @cloudflare/vite-plugin 1.37.1, vinext 0.0.50, react-server-dom-webpack 19.2.6, next ^16.2.12 — all flagged as DIRECT); deploy/railway/serve.mjs:126-150 (production = `npx wrangler dev`, so devDependencies are the serving process); repo root (no .github/, no renovate.json or dependabot config)
findings.evidence: `npm audit --json` on 2026-09-10: {"low":1,"moderate":8,"high":15,"critical":1,"total":25} (saved to scratchpad/critic/npm-audit.json). High advisories inside the serving process: ws 'uninitialized memory disclosure' and 'memory exhaustion DoS from tiny fragments', undici 'HTTP header injection via Set-Cookie percent-decoding' and 'TLS certificate validation bypass', miniflare/wrangler via those. The critical is next (Image Optimization RCE advisories) — nominal here because vinext/workerd is the runtime, but the package still ships. Fixes exist without a major bump for @cloudflare/vite-plugin 1.54.6, vite 8.3.0, react-server-dom-webpack 19.3.0, next patch; vinext needs 1.0.0-beta.9 (major). tsc --noEmit and eslint both exit 0 (scratchpad/critic/tsc.txt, eslint.txt).
findings.impact: A public SaaS whose HTTP runtime carries published DoS and memory-disclosure advisories, and nobody is notified when new ones land; the fix for infra-16 (wrangler dev in prod) makes this worse until the runtime is pinned and updated on a cadence.
findings.recommendation: Run `npm audit fix` for the non-major set now and pin wrangler to the patched line; add Dependabot (or Renovate) with weekly grouped PRs; when CI exists (infra-11) add `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` plus a separate check for the runtime packages since they are devDependencies here.

findings.title: No per-user storage quota and no rate limit on authenticated API routes: one verified free account can fill the single Railway volume (D1 + R2 blobs + auth.db + session secret) with 10 MB uploads and take the product down for everyone
findings.location: app/api/evidence/_shared.ts:8-9 (MAX_EVIDENCE_BYTES 10 MB, MAX_EVIDENCE_PER_ACTIVITY 12 — no per-user total); app/api/evidence/route.ts:94-97, 111, 152, 166 (content-length check, formData(), arrayBuffer() — whole file buffered); app/api/workspace/route.ts (createCredential/addActivity/createPersonalTask: no per-account ceilings; grep MAX_|quota|per user = 0); deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:95-124 (proxy has no limiter; limiters exist only for /auth/* and Basic failures); Dockerfile:4 and serve.mjs PERSIST_DIR (everything durable lives under /data)
findings.evidence: No SUM(size_bytes) or quota query exists anywhere in app/api/evidence or route.ts. Railway service_metrics (24 h, prod): DISK_USAGE_GB 1.13, MEMORY_USAGE_GB 1.42 idle, CPU ~0.002; the volume's capacity is not exposed by the API. Uploads are 10 MB × 12 per activity × unlimited activities, and /api/* has no throttle, so a 20-line script can write gigabytes per minute once email (infra-01) lets anyone verify.
findings.impact: Disk-full on the shared volume fails SQLite/D1 writes and the auth store for every user at once, and that volume is also the only copy of all data (infra-04). This is the cheapest denial-of-service against the product and it needs only a free account.
findings.recommendation: Enforce a per-user byte quota (SUM(size_bytes) over evidence_files before the R2 put; e.g. 250 MB) and per-account record ceilings; add a token-bucket limiter keyed by session/IP for /api/* in the gateway; stream uploads instead of arrayBuffer(); set a disk-usage alert at 70% and separate blobs from the database (real R2 or a second volume).

findings.title: No error telemetry anywhere: no client error/unhandledrejection handler, no server error reporter, and the Railway log API currently returns nothing for the live deployment, so the P1 crash and every 500 are invisible to the team
findings.location: app/ITrackApp.tsx (no window 'error' / 'unhandledrejection' listeners, no ErrorBoundary); app/api/workspace/route.ts errorResponse (~12478-12500: console.error only); deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:224-232 (console.error only); app/, deploy/, worker/ (no Sentry/OTel/beacon); Railway service itrack, deployment b8b32146-d274-475a-9bfc-2d6c18fe28f4
findings.evidence: grep -rniE 'sentry|bugsnag|telemetry|errorReport|window.onerror|unhandledrejection' app deploy worker → 0 hits. Railway get_logs(deploy, level=error, since 7d) and get_logs(deploy, search '[auth]', since 30d) both returned 'No Deploy logs found for deployment b8b32146…', so even the console fallback (the only place verification links land today, infra-15) is not retrievable through the API. HTTP logs for the last 2 days show only scanner traffic (/.env variants, phpinfo, wp-includes) and no real-user paths.
findings.impact: A self-serve product with no feedback loop: the log-activity crash shipped to prod unnoticed, signups/pushes/500s fail silently, and landing-auth-M-07 (funnel metrics) only covers the happy path. Nobody will learn about the next regression until a user emails a bouncing support address.
findings.recommendation: Add a React error boundary (architecture-M-02) that also POSTs the stack to a tiny /api/client-error endpoint; register window 'error' and 'unhandledrejection' beacons; give server errors a request id and a structured log line; forward logs to a free Sentry/Axiom/Better Stack project and alert on error rate and on zero traffic.

findings.title: Rule-content governance is undefined: all 170 templates share one blanket LAST_VERIFIED_AT = "2026-07-26" constant per file, every template is the same review status, there is no re-verification cadence, owner, changelog, or in-product 'this template changed' signal, and existing credentials keep their snapshot silently until renewal
findings.location: db/catalog/*.ts (11 files each declare `const LAST_VERIFIED_AT = "2026-07-26"`; reviewStatus is 'source_linked_check_conditions' in all 102 occurrences); app/ITrackApp.tsx:562-575 (ruleReviewLabel has a 'verified' state that no catalog row uses); app/api/workspace/route.ts:9724-9760 (newer_rule guard only at cycle rollover for some families) and 0 client strings for 'newer template'/'template updated'; docs/ (no maintenance or review process document); README.md:41-52 ('170 current, source-linked templates')
findings.evidence: grep LAST_VERIFIED_AT db/catalog → 11 identical constants; grep of dated literals shows 23 × '2026-07-26' and the rest are effective dates; grep -rhoE 'reviewStatus: "[a-z_]+"' → one value only; the NREMT family I spot-checked matches the real 2025 NCCP model (EMR 16 = 8/4/4, EMT 40, etc.) and links primary sources, so content quality is good today — but it is 6.5 weeks old with no mechanism to age it, and a rule edit in the catalog reaches an existing credential only through the rollover guard.
findings.impact: The rules are the product and the liability: a board changes a requirement, the template stays 'source-linked' with a green-looking date, and users plan a cycle against stale minimums. The landing page (landing-auth-09) is about to advertise source-linked rules with review dates; that promise needs a process behind it.
findings.recommendation: Make lastVerifiedAt per rule with a reviewer field; put a quarterly review calendar and a CHANGELOG.md of rule changes in the repo; surface 'Rules reviewed <date> · <source>' on the credential screen and age it visually past 6 months; when a newer version exists for a credential's stable_key, emit a check-in ('Template updated — review your plan') instead of waiting for renewal; add a test that fails when any template's lastVerifiedAt is older than N days at build time.

findings.title: Data portability is one-directional and partial: CSV export covers non-archived activities only (no credentials, tasks, check-in state, or evidence files), there is no import at all, and architecture-M-03's 'no data export' is overstated
findings.location: app/api/export/route.ts:44-83 (activities WHERE archived_at IS NULL; 10 columns) and :112; app/api/export/packet/route.ts (per-credential HTML packet); app/ITrackApp.tsx:8446 (History 'Export CSV', disabled until a credential exists), :7569 and :8092 (packet links); app/api/workspace/route.ts:12377-12459 (no import/bulk action); fresh-user History screenshot critic/fresh-desktop-history.png
findings.evidence: The export route exists and is linked from History (contradicting the 'no data export' wording in architecture-M-03), but it emits only activity rows; evidence blobs are reachable one at a time via /api/evidence/[id]; there is no credentials/tasks/reminders export and no CSV/JSON import. A new user with a spreadsheet of 5 years of CE must retype every row through the 19-control sheet (app-ux-06).
findings.impact: Onboarding friction for exactly the people most likely to convert (professionals mid-cycle with existing records), incomplete GDPR/CCPA-style portability, and a lock-in that users of a free tool will resent when they leave.
findings.recommendation: Ship a full export (JSON + evidence files as a zip, or a packet per credential plus a CSV per table) and a CSV import for activities with a preview step; keep the CSV formula-injection guard (csvCell) — it is correct.

findings.title: Gateway makes routing decisions on a parsed pathname but proxies the raw request-target: `//`-prefixed URLs are classified as `/` or as sibling routes, so the /internal, /cdn-cgi and /__scheduled blocklist and the page routes can be reached under a different classification (live on prod)
findings.location: deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:127-128 (`new URL(req.url ?? '/', 'http://placeholder')` — a `//host/path` target parses as host+path), :136-144 (blocklist tests url.pathname), :175-178 and :202-209 (page/landing decisions on pathname), :110 (`path: req.url` proxies the raw target); worker/index.ts:136 (worker still matches `url.pathname === '/internal/run-scheduled'` and requires the per-boot secret)
findings.evidence: Prod GETs on 2026-09-10 with a Safari UA and Accept: text/html: /internal/run-scheduled → 404; //internal/run-scheduled → 303 /login; /cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled → 404; //cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled → 303 /login; //xmlrpc.php → 200 (7,723-byte landing page); //login → 200 landing. With Accept: application/json, //internal/run-scheduled → 401 Basic instead of 404. Railway HTTP log 2026-09-10T14:06:57Z: 'GET //xmlrpc.php 200'. No exploit today because the worker re-checks the exact pathname and the internal secret is random per boot.
findings.impact: Every gateway rule the other findings ask for (public-asset allowlist, robots/sitemap, path-keyed security headers, the JSON-401 split) inherits the mismatch: a request can be judged as one path and forwarded as another. It is a footgun, not a breach — yet.
findings.recommendation: Reject request-targets that do not start with exactly one '/' (`if (!req.url.startsWith('/') || req.url.startsWith('//')) return 400`), proxy `url.pathname + url.search` rather than req.url, and add a gateway test for the `//` form alongside the UA-gate tests being rewritten.

findings.title: Cross-tenant isolation holds in a live probe but is untested: no automated test exercises two identities against /api/workspace, /api/evidence, or /api/export/packet, right before a 12,500-line route decomposition
findings.location: tests/ (only one identity is ever used: tests/rendered-html.test.mjs:305 sets a single oai-authenticated-user-email; auth-gateway tests are gateway-level); app/api/workspace/route.ts:12377-12459 (23 actions all take ids from the payload); app/api/evidence/_shared.ts:157-200 (findOwnedEvidence scopes by user_id); README.md:35 ('server-derived ownership')
findings.evidence: Live probe on the dev worker as critic-fresh@example.com against the demo user's ids (scratchpad/critic/critic-idor2.json): archiveActivity → 404 activity_not_found; updateActivity → 404; setReminderState → 404 credential_not_found; addActivityAllocation → 404; createPersonalTask → 404; GET /api/export/packet?credentialId=demo → 404; GET /api/evidence?activityId=demo → 200 {"evidence":[]} (scoped, leaks nothing); demo state afterwards unchanged (revision 2, 3 tasks, 1 allocation). POST bodies without expectedRevision fail validation before the ownership check, which is fine. Nothing in tests/ asserts any of this.
findings.impact: The ownership scoping is correct by construction today but only by convention; the planned decomposition of route.ts (architecture-M-05) and the screen-file split are exactly the refactors that regress `WHERE user_id = ?` clauses with nothing to catch it.
findings.recommendation: Before moving code, add a two-identity isolation suite: for every action in the dispatch switch and every GET route, replay a valid payload with foreign ids and assert 404/403 and an unchanged workspace; keep it in the same file the decomposition touches so it cannot be skipped.

themes.theme: One root cause reported ~20 ways: the WKWebView-era gateway gate (UA/Accept gate + HTTP Basic + 401 Basic on JSON + widget bypass)
themes.note: All of these close with one gateway PR (~150 lines in gateway.mjs/serve.mjs plus rewriting tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs): delete Basic auth, the UA gate, the widget bypass and ITRACK_USERS/ITRACK_OPEN_IDENTITY; serve landing/303 for HTML and a JSON 401 for the API; allowlist public assets; normalise the request-target (critic-07). Deleting Basic also retires the live path for the committed password (infra-03) — still rotate it wherever reused and purge git history — and closes security-05 and ios-coupling-M-02 for free.

themes.theme: Email + DNS is the launch gate, and four findings are the same two env vars
themes.note: RESEND_API_KEY + AUTH_EMAIL_FROM + PUBLIC_BASE_URL on Railway and SPF/DKIM/DMARC/MX at Name.com are Chris-owned; nothing else in the funnel can be verified until they exist. The link-in-logs findings become moot only when email works AND the console.log in deliver() is removed. Note that today no verification link can reach anyone, and the Railway log API returned nothing for the live deployment (critic-04), so even the documented 'read the link from the logs' fallback is currently unusable.

themes.theme: Verification/recovery flow must be redesigned as one unit — two of the surviving fixes conflict
themes.note: Implementing landing-auth-M-02 naively (re-send the link when an unverified email signs up again) amplifies security-M-01 (the squatter's password survives and the real owner verifies it for them). The consistent design: a repeat signup of an unverified email REPLACES password and name and re-sends; /verify shows a page with a POST confirm button instead of consuming the token on GET; every outcome says 'check your email' (which also resolves the enumeration findings that pull against the specific-message UX findings).

themes.theme: Sign out is one bug reported four times; account self-service and the split identity are its siblings
themes.note: The fix is a POST form to the existing /auth/logout (the CSRF check requires an Origin, so it cannot stay an <a href>), plus re-issuing the cookie on activity so the 30-day session actually slides. Account deletion/email change must delete across three stores (auth.db, D1 rows keyed by sha256(email), R2 blobs) — architecture-M-03 is right about the design, but its 'no data export' wording is overstated (see critic-06).

themes.theme: The crash, the missing boundary, and the missing telemetry are one story
themes.note: The crash is a five-line fix (read event.currentTarget.value before calling setActivityDraft). architecture-16 is a P1 that reports zero instances — it is a convention note and inflates the P1 count; downgrade it. Without an error boundary and an error beacon (critic-04) the next crash will again be found by an audit rather than by the team.

themes.theme: Public-page hygiene: headers, SEO, brand, contrast, pricing copy
themes.note: The five HTML pages are being rewritten in the redesign, so contrast/structure/brand findings are inputs to that rewrite; but HSTS/security headers, robots/sitemap/favicon, www DNS, and removing the pricing copy plus the tests that pin it (landing-auth-08, architecture-18) are gateway/DNS work that should ship now.

themes.theme: Overlay, focus, inert, and title behaviour — the same primitives reported by app-ux and a11y separately
themes.note: One Modal and one screen-stack primitive own all of these. Build them once in the redesign's shared component, but `inert` on the parked screen and document.title per route are small enough to ship immediately.

themes.theme: Monolith decomposition is blocked by test coupling and needs an isolation net first
themes.note: 165 source-regex assertions plus ~130 iOS-UI markup assertions in tests/rendered-html.test.mjs fail on any file move, so delete or rewrite them before the first screen file is extracted; add the two-identity isolation suite (critic-08) before touching route.ts. tsc and eslint are clean today, which makes the split cheaper than the file sizes suggest.

themes.theme: iOS residue removal set — delete, don't refactor, in the order ios-coupling-14 gives
themes.note: security-01 (widget feed leaking the oldest account) is the only live data leak in the set and goes first; APNs code/tables/env and the .p8 revocation go last; ios-coupling-10 is the keep-list (manifest, SW, web push, safe-area) and must be honoured in the same PRs. Product decision 1 makes every one of these fix_regardless.

themes.theme: Ops floor for a public SaaS — all missing, none visible to users until it fails
themes.note: No backup, no uptime check on a real route, no CI, no staging, no dependency updates, no quotas, no telemetry, and a single volume holding D1 + R2 + auth.db + the cookie secret. Railway shows 1.13 GB used and 1.4 GB RSS idle for a process with ~0 CPU. Every item here is Chris-owned or a small script; none is a redesign question.

themes.theme: Home/credential model and copy — the data-model gaps hiding among visual findings
themes.note: Three items in this group are not visual and must not wait for the redesign: credential edit/delete/archive actions (app-ux-03), correct current-cycle selection after renewal (app-ux-04), and local-date/time-zone defaults (critic-01). Fixing them first stops the redesign from encoding UTC 'today' and single-credential assumptions into new screens.

themes.theme: Rules are the product: nobody audited rule governance
themes.note: The 170 templates are good (the NREMT family matches the 2025 NCCP model and cites primary sources) but carry one blanket review date and no maintenance process; the landing page is about to promise 'source-linked rules with review dates', the chooser is a 170-option select, and the catalog is a 700 KB payload — three findings about the same asset with no owner.

themes.theme: Overstated or misfiled findings to re-grade before planning
themes.note: architecture-16 is a P1 with zero instances; architecture-M-03 says 'no data export' but CSV and packet exports exist (the real gap is completeness, critic-06); ios-coupling-13 restates infra-01/security-M-02 as a dependency; infra-17 is a checklist, not a finding; app-ux-04 is a logic bug, arguably P2. After de-duplication the genuine P1 set is: email unconfigured, the gateway gate, the log-activity crash, dead sign-out, the widget-feed leak, the committed password, no backups, and no credential edit/delete.

Summary: the eight dimensions are thorough on the funnel, the gateway and the client shell, but thin on the domain core — nobody checked date/time-zone semantics, rule-content governance, abuse limits, dependency health, error telemetry, or cross-tenant isolation, and about a third of the surviving list is duplicates of three root causes (gateway gate, email, sign out). My spot checks: the UTC-'today' bug is confirmed with a faked clock; cross-tenant isolation held in a live probe of seven actions; tsc and eslint are clean; npm audit shows 25 advisories including the production runtime; prod HTTP logs show only scanner traffic and the deploy-log API returns nothing; the fresh-user zero state is coherent (Home first-run is good, Profile front-loads gamification and a dead sign-out link). Nothing I found displaces the top of the queue — email, gateway, and the crash/sign-out triage remain first — but time-zone correctness, quotas, and telemetry belong in the launch set rather than the polish list. Assets (all under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-chrisskerritt/b54a3ee3-2931-4be9-852c-12276d32d9b1/scratchpad/): critic/critic-probe.json, critic/clock-log-sheet.png, critic/clock-home-desktop.png, critic/fresh-desktop-{home,credentials,history,profile}.png, critic/fresh-mobile-{home,credentials,history,profile}.png, critic/critic-idor.json, critic/critic-idor2.json, critic/npm-audit.json, critic/tsc.txt, critic/eslint.txt; scripts pw/critic-probe.mjs, pw/critic-idor.mjs, pw/critic-idor2.mjs. Dev-data footprint: one user row critic-fresh@example.com created in the local dev D1 (no records), nothing on prod.

fix_first.what: Turn on email and fix the domain: RESEND_API_KEY, AUTH_EMAIL_FROM, PUBLIC_BASE_URL on Railway; SPF/DKIM/DMARC and an MX (or forwarding) for support@ at Name.com; then remove the console.log of raw links in deliver().
fix_first.why: Nothing in the self-serve funnel can be verified, recovered, or supported until this exists (infra-01/-02, security-M-02/-M-03/-M-04, landing-auth-01); it is entirely Chris-owned configuration, blocks retiring ITRACK_USERS, and every downstream funnel finding is untestable without it.

fix_first.what: One gateway PR: delete HTTP Basic, the UA/Accept gate, the widget bypass and ITRACK_USERS/OPEN_IDENTITY; serve landing/303 for HTML and a JSON 401 for /api; allowlist robots/sitemap/favicon/manifest/og; add HSTS + security headers; normalise `//` request-targets; rewrite tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs. Then rotate and purge the committed password.
fix_first.why: It closes ~20 surviving findings and the only live data leak (security-01) in one change, unblocks link previews, crawlers, HEAD checks and the installed PWA, removes the brute-force surface, and ends the native Basic dialog that greets every expired session.

fix_first.what: App triage PR shipped before any redesign work: read event.currentTarget.value before the five setActivityDraft updaters; add an error boundary plus a client error beacon; replace the /signout-with-chatgpt link with a POST form to /auth/logout and re-issue the session cookie on activity; set inert on the parked screen and document.title per route.
fix_first.why: These are the P1 core-flow breakages (crash, no sign-out) plus two ten-line accessibility fixes; all are fix_regardless, none conflict with the redesign, and the beacon means the next regression is seen by the team instead of by an auditor.

fix_first.what: Public-SaaS floor: scheduled Railway volume backups with a tested restore; an external uptime check on a real route; per-user storage quota and an /api rate limit; npm audit fixes plus Dependabot; a CI job that runs the existing tests and typecheck on PRs.
fix_first.why: Today one hostile signup can fill the single volume that holds every user's data with no backup, no alert and no notice; these are small scripts and dashboard settings, and they are the difference between a hobby deployment and something strangers can be invited to.

fix_first.what: Fix the three data-model gaps the redesign would otherwise inherit: local-date/time-zone defaults with automatic device time-zone capture (critic-01), credential edit/delete/archive actions (app-ux-03), and current-cycle selection after a renewal is accepted (app-ux-04) — with a two-identity isolation test suite added first (critic-08).
fix_first.why: These are API and helper changes, not visuals; new screens will consume the same helpers and actions, so fixing them before decomposition keeps UTC 'today', permanent mistakes, and closed-cycle countdowns from being rebuilt into the redesign, and the isolation suite protects the 12,500-line route through the refactor.
